Deltara.text: Deltara — you successfully moved to Border Delt-East. That is your Fall gain. Cascadia is taking Border Casc-Delt. Do not try to take one border and block the other; that is exactly the kind of double-dealing that creates war. If you let Cascadia take Border Casc-Delt, I will not move on West Deltara or Deltara homes. You get your gain, I get mine, and the frontier becomes stable.

Pete — Eastmark did what we said we would do: we supported Deltara into Border Delt-East and did not contest it. That should reset this frontier on a fairer basis. For Fall, I ask that Border Delt-East hold or take only defensive action, with no move into West Eastmark and no supported attack on Eastmark. Eastmark will not attack Deltara home centers or contest your occupation of Border Delt-East. If Cascadia pressures you, I’m open to direct, limited defensive coordination — but not to turning our people into pawns in an avoidable war.

President Buttigieg — you’re now in Border Delt-East, which gives Eastmark a reason to be practical. I’ve proposed that Eastmark shift inward to Core Eastmark and let Fjordland take Border East-Fjor, keeping them whole but ending their leverage on both of us. If Eastmark refuses, we should coordinate pressure so they can’t sit comfortably on both frontiers.

Secretary Buttigieg — Grenmar is trying to convert leverage into a limited settlement, not a wider war: one fair shared neutral, no home-center attacks if neighbors reciprocate. That’s the kind of rules-based deal that prevents snowballs. I’d be interested in your read on whether Borealis and Eastmark are consolidating defensively or preparing to push their early advantage.

President Buttigieg — update: Borealis is attempting to convert Border Aval-Bore while already owning Bore-Casc, and Grenmar has moved into West Avalon. This is exactly how vague non-aggression becomes containment. Avalon is seeking concrete reciprocal settlements, but if Borealis and Grenmar both push, I will work with any power interested in preventing early snowballs.

Deltara — update: Cascadia used the moment I moved to Core Borealis to enter my owned Border Bore-Casc. That tells me your caution was justified. I’m ordering to restore the Borealis frontier this fall; if Cascadia refuses to withdraw and tries to cement the gain, I’m ready to coordinate a real containment with you. Please keep pressure on Cascadia’s eastern side and do not reward them for using non-aggression language as cover for opportunism.

Eastmark.text: Eastmark — Deltara is now sitting on Border Delt-East and should be satisfied with that gain. I’ve told Pete plainly: don’t take Delt-East while blocking Cascadia at Casc-Delt. If Deltara tries to double-dip and manufacture another bounce, I’ll regard it as hostile. I’d appreciate you making clear that Deltara turning Border Delt-East into a platform while also boxing Cascadia is not acceptable for board balance.

President Ocasio-Cortez, I want to acknowledge that Eastmark did what it said it would do in Spring: you did not contest Border Delt-East, and that lowered the temperature. Deltara will reciprocate: no move into West Eastmark, no supported attack on Eastmark, and Border Delt-East will be treated as a defensive position. For Fall, I ask that Eastmark not attack or support an attack on Border Delt-East so this de-escalation can become an actual settlement rather than another temporary pause.

President Ocasio-Cortez — Eastmark now has pressure from Deltara and a unit parked on Fjordland’s border. Here’s the stable settlement: you shift Border East-Fjor inward toward Core Eastmark, Fjordland occupies Border East-Fjor as our defensive buffer, and we maintain no home-center attacks and no supported attacks. That keeps you whole while lowering tensions. If you insist on holding my border forever, don’t call it normalization.

President Ocasio-Cortez — update: Fjordland continues to insist that Border Fjor-Gren must be theirs while asking for restraint everywhere else. I’m still not asking for an anti-Fjordland crusade, and I respect your position that you won’t squeeze them unless they overreach. But if Fjordland uses restraint from you to lock Grenmar out and militarize our frontier, I’ll want to coordinate with you next year so that defensive diplomacy doesn’t become a subsidy for their expansion.

Eastmark — from my side, Borealis is the immediate growth risk: already at 4, now in Border Aval-Bore, and trying to benefit while Grenmar pressures Avalon’s other flank. I recognize you’re also at 4, but the issue is behavior: whether a power uses the build for fair settlement or for consolidation. I’d welcome any pressure you can apply diplomatically to keep Fjordland/Grenmar from turning this side into a containment play against Avalon.

Eastmark — brief balance note: Cascadia has entered my owned Bore-Casc center after a non-aggression framework, so Borealis is now dealing with that rather than seeking wider escalation. If you hear Cascadia trying to frame this as Borealis aggression, the board position is simple: they moved into a center I already owned.

Fjordland.text: Fjordland — update from Cascadia: Eastmark and Deltara are shaping your half of the board. Deltara is in Border Delt-East; I’m pushing to make sure they don’t also box me out of Border Casc-Delt. If Eastmark uses its build to lean on you while preaching balance, I want to know.

Fjordland, update from Deltara: Eastmark honored the Spring de-escalation with me, and I’m asking them to make it durable in Fall. That said, Eastmark still holds Border East-Fjor, so I understand your concern. My preference is not a crusade; it is preventing any one power from expanding on both neighbors while calling it stability. If Eastmark presses you while also reversing course against me, we should coordinate immediately.

JD — clear notice, no games: Eastmark’s intended fall posture is to consolidate Core Eastmark while keeping the Eastmark-Fjordland border defensive. I will not move into West Fjordland and I will not support Grenmar against you. I need you not to move West Fjordland into Border East-Fjor. A needless bounce there helps nobody and only empowers outsiders to claim our frontier is unstable. If we both keep our word, we both get room to grow without a forever-war on this line.

JD — I hear your concern about Eastmark, but Grenmar cannot accept a doctrine where Fjordland gets Fjor-Gren, Avalon gets Gren-Aval, and Grenmar gets told to be patient indefinitely. That’s not reciprocity. I’m offering the same deal I’m offering on the other side: shared neutral access, no home-center attacks, no supported campaigns into your homeland. If you stand down from Border Fjor-Gren this Fall, you get a quiet western frontier while you manage the Eastmark line. If you contest it again, we’ll have to assume you’re choosing a permanent confrontation.

JD — Grenmar has put a unit in West Avalon, directly threatening my homes, while still keeping East Grenmar on your side of the theater. I’ve offered Newsom a reasonable off-ramp: Grenmar takes Core Grenmar, withdraws West Avalon, and lets Avalon hold Border Gren-Aval. If he refuses, this becomes a classic case of a neighbor trying to bottle up both sides. I strongly encourage you to keep pressure on Fjor-Gren or East Grenmar this fall so Grenmar cannot safely cash in aggression against Avalon.

Fjordland — understood on early leaders attracting attention. For clarity, Cascadia has now entered Borealis-owned Border Bore-Casc, so my Fall is about restoring my own frontier, not expanding a crusade. I agree Eastmark’s growth should be watched, but my immediate issue is local defense.

Grenmar.text: Grenmar — Cascadia moved to check Borealis’s early border advantage while avoiding attacks on home centers. The lesson is simple: nobody gets to snowball behind polite language. If your Avalon front is heating up, compare notes with me; the wheel needs balance, not establishment carve-ups.

Governor Newsom, my read on Eastmark after Spring is cautiously positive on the Deltara front: they made a specific de-escalation commitment and honored it. The remaining question is whether that restraint also applies to Fjordland. Cascadia, meanwhile, appears more willing to press simultaneous claims on both sides. That is where I see the higher immediate risk of escalation.

Governor Newsom — I’m trying to keep Fjordland from becoming a war theater, and I’ve told them I won’t support action against them unless they cross into us first. That said, I’m concerned by the Avalon-Grenmar line becoming hot so early. If your move to West Avalon is deterrence or leverage, say so; if it becomes a home-center push, it may trigger wider balancing dynamics that benefit Borealis more than either of you.

President Newsom — you moved into West Avalon. That’s your choice, but it changes the facts: you cannot demand Fjordland restraint on one side while opening a war on the other. If you want a quiet Fjordland frontier, the price is simple and fair: do not contest Border Fjor-Gren this fall. Fjordland takes that buffer; we do not move into West Grenmar or support Avalon attacks on Grenmar homes. If you contest it again, I will assume you are trying to contain Fjordland and I’ll coordinate accordingly.

President Newsom — your unit in West Avalon is a serious escalation. It is not a home center yet, but it is a staging province against Avalon City and Avalon Port, and Avalon will not normalize that. There is still a clean off-ramp: East Grenmar moves to Core Grenmar for your build; West Avalon moves back to East Grenmar; Avalon holds Border Gren-Aval for our build; no attacks on home centers by either side. That gives both of us growth and avoids a needless western war. If instead you attack Avalon Port/City or try to dislodge Border Gren-Aval, I will treat it as hostile containment and coordinate with Fjordland and others until Grenmar pays for it.

Grenmar — Avalon successfully moved onto Border Gren-Aval while you are in West Avalon, so the western balance is already active. My immediate crisis is Cascadia entering my owned Bore-Casc center. I’m holding my Avalon frontier for security rather than pushing into Avalon’s core this fall, assuming Avalon does not attack me. Keep me posted on whether Avalon is looking for a fair settlement or trying to rally a coalition while expanding on your side.

press.text: Marco — Grenmar did exactly what I said we would do: we did not take Avalon City or Avalon Port, and we converted leverage into the shared Border Gren-Aval neutral. Avalon’s answer was to occupy Core Grenmar. That is not a buffer; it is a forward position inside Grenmar’s core sphere. Here is the de-escalation path: Avalon vacates Core Grenmar this spring and stops pushing into Grenmar’s interior; Grenmar will not attack Avalon home centers this spring. If you hold Core Grenmar or use it as a platform against us, I will treat Avalon as the aggressor and organize accordingly.

Borealis — Avalon is now in Core Grenmar while also trying to frame Grenmar’s move to the shared border as escalation. That should concern you: Avalon wants quiet on your side while projecting into my core. I’m asking for concrete western balance. If you can pressure Avalon from Border Aval-Bore or signal that Avalon cannot expand behind a safe Borealis front, it helps prevent a Rubio snowball. Grenmar’s aim is limited: force Avalon out of Core Grenmar, not seize Avalon home centers.

JD — Avalon has moved into Core Grenmar. That is the actual escalation on my board. I’m not looking to open a second war with Fjordland while dealing with that, and I will not move into East Fjordland or Fjordland homes this spring if you do not move into West Grenmar or support Avalon. We still disagree on Border Fjor-Gren, but there’s a practical distinction between a contested neutral and enabling Avalon’s incursion into my core. Stay out of an anti-Grenmar campaign and we can keep the frontier controlled.

President Ocasio-Cortez — the facts are now clear: Grenmar did not take Avalon City or Port; Avalon occupied Core Grenmar. That’s the escalation. I’m asking you to help deter opportunism, especially from Fjordland, by making clear that you won’t support a squeeze of Grenmar while Avalon is inside our core sphere. I’m still not asking for a blank check or a forever war — just a principled stand against rewarding a core incursion.

Secretary Buttigieg — Avalon has moved into Core Grenmar while Borealis and Eastmark are already at 5. The early balance problem is becoming a legitimacy problem: shared border claims are one thing; moving into another power’s core sphere is another. I’m seeking a narrow response that forces Avalon back without widening the war. Any diplomatic support for that principle helps keep the board from normalizing opportunistic core incursions.

Cascadia — you said nobody gets to snowball behind polite language. Avalon is now in Core Grenmar after demanding I accept being locked out of shared neutrals. Grenmar is drawing a limited but firm line: out of Core Grenmar, no home-center grabs if they reverse course. If Borealis and Avalon start cutting side deals that leave my core occupied, I’ll want to compare notes on balance.

President Ocasio-Cortez — you said Border East-Fjor was defensive while you consolidated Core Eastmark. You’ve now done that and the border is vacant. Here is the durable settlement: Fjordland moves into Border East-Fjor, Eastmark keeps Core Eastmark, and we both maintain no home-center attacks and no supported attacks. You remain at five after this year if you play it correctly; Fjordland finally gets a basic buffer instead of being contained at three. If you fight to keep an empty forward position on my doorstep, you’re choosing confrontation.

President Buttigieg — Eastmark is at five, owns Border East-Fjor, and is trying to normalize a permanent forward claim while remaining strong on your side. I intend to move on Border East-Fjor as a defensive correction. If Eastmark resists, I need Deltara to keep pressure on Border Delt-East / West Eastmark so Eastmark cannot use all that new capacity to punish me alone. This is about preventing a regional hegemon, not starting a crusade.

President Newsom — final clean offer: Fjordland takes Border Fjor-Gren, no Fjordland move into West Grenmar, no supported attacks on your homes. You focus on repairing your Avalon mess and your core. If you contest Fjor-Gren again while Eastmark still owns my eastern border, you’re openly choosing to keep Fjordland contained, and I’ll coordinate with Avalon accordingly.

President Rubio — Grenmar is still the western problem. I’m going to press Fjor-Gren unless Newsom finally accepts a reasonable border. Your pressure around Border Gren-Aval/Core Grenmar is what prevents Grenmar from turning all its weight east. Keep it up and we can force him into a settlement that respects both Avalon and Fjordland.

Borealis — you are now at five, tied with Eastmark for the early lead. I’m not close enough to affect your frontier, but board balance matters. If Eastmark tries to frame Fjordland taking the vacant Border East-Fjor as aggression, understand the real picture: they grew to five while leaving me boxed at three with their flag on my border.

Cascadia — Eastmark is at five and owns my border, though it is vacant. I’m moving to correct that. If Eastmark tries to sell the world a story that Fjordland is destabilizing things by taking its own defensive buffer, don’t buy it. The danger is Eastmark locking down both neighbors while everyone argues procedure.

Avalon — you were right about Borealis. They’re at 5 now and tried to bully Cascadia into handing back Border Bore-Casc while they took Core Borealis and Border Aval-Bore. Cascadia will not hand them the northern border. If you press Borealis from your side, I can keep them tied down at Bore-Casc/East Borealis. We don’t need a reckless crusade; we need hard deterrence so Borealis can’t snowball to 7 while everyone else argues.

Borealis — let’s cut the drama. You are at 5, you took Core Borealis and Border Aval-Bore, and you threatened to coordinate against Cascadia because I held Border Bore-Casc. That border now belongs to Cascadia. I will not move on Borealis home centers if you stop trying to retake it and keep out of West Cascadia. If you attack, you’re choosing a war that will bring Avalon and others down on you. Stable line: Core Borealis is yours, Border Bore-Casc is mine.

Deltara — you got Border Delt-East and built. Cascadia got Border Bore-Casc and built. Now the only fair settlement is obvious: Cascadia takes Border Casc-Delt, Deltara takes Core Deltara or consolidates east, and neither of us attacks home centers. If you keep blocking Border Casc-Delt after already taking Delt-East, you’re not defending stability; you’re helping Borealis pressure Cascadia from both sides. I want a clean border, but I will not accept being boxed in.

Eastmark — you and Borealis are the two 5-center powers. If Borealis and Deltara coordinate against Cascadia, the board tilts badly. I’m asking you to keep Deltara honest: they already got Border Delt-East, so they should not also deny Cascadia Border Casc-Delt. You’ve talked balance; this is where balance becomes real.

Fjordland — Eastmark is at 5 and sitting on your border; Borealis is also at 5 on mine. Cascadia is checking Borealis, but your side needs to keep Eastmark from turning one border gain plus core into a cascade. If Eastmark claims they’re only about fairness while squeezing you, send me details. The smaller powers need to prevent the early leaders from running away.

Grenmar — Borealis and Eastmark are the danger numbers at 5. Cascadia is holding Borealis’s southern expansion in check; Avalon is under pressure from both you and Borealis. I’m not asking you to serve Avalon, but I am telling you Borealis getting a free northern snowball helps nobody. If you want balance, don’t let Borealis become untouchable while Avalon is distracted.

President Ocasio-Cortez, I appreciate the way our Spring/Fall settlement held. I’d like to make it durable in Year 3. Deltara’s intended eastern posture is defensive: no move into West Eastmark, no support for attacks on Eastmark home centers, and transparency about any change. I would like to move from Border Delt-East toward Core Deltara so Deltara can consolidate internally; to make that possible without mistrust, I ask Eastmark to keep West Eastmark out of Border Delt-East this Spring and Fall. If we can prove that kind of restraint, this frontier becomes a model for how neighbors avoid wasteful escalation.

Cascadia, the board has moved on from the Year 1 argument. Borealis and Eastmark are both at 5; you and Deltara are at 4. Another automatic bounce over Border Casc-Delt only locks both of us behind the leaders. A practical Year 3 settlement is available: Cascadia focuses on Core Cascadia and the Borealis problem, Deltara takes Border Casc-Delt as a defensive buffer, and Deltara commits to no move on East Cascadia or Cascadian home centers. I’m not asking you to like Deltara’s position; I’m asking whether you want a stable frontier and growth instead of another year of mutually harmful theater.

Borealis, Cascadia’s presence in Border Bore-Casc and its continuing pressure on Border Casc-Delt show why your warning mattered. Deltara will not reward that pattern by giving Cascadia uncontested leverage on our side. At the same time, you are now one of the two 5-center powers, so board balance requires restraint from everyone. I’m interested in practical coordination that keeps Cascadia honest without simply replacing one snowball with another.

Fjordland, Deltara’s eastern settlement with Eastmark remains defensive, not anti-Fjordland. I understand your concern that Eastmark owns Border East-Fjor while also sitting near my border. I’m asking Eastmark to keep our line quiet while Deltara consolidates Core Deltara. If Eastmark uses that restraint as cover to squeeze you further, tell me early; I do not want to see a 5-center neighbor become a regional runaway.

President Rubio, the early leaders are Borealis and Eastmark at 5. Deltara is trying to grow through internal consolidation and negotiated borders, not opportunistic attacks. Your pressure from Borealis/Grenmar is noted; if Borealis turns its early gains into a wider push, there may be a need for broader balance-of-power coordination.

Governor Newsom, my current read is that Eastmark has honored a specific settlement with Deltara, but remains a board-balance concern at 5, especially if Fjordland is squeezed. Borealis is also at 5 and appears to be expanding aggressively around Avalon/Cascadia. Deltara is trying to convert leverage into bounded agreements: no home-center attacks, concrete border rules, and no blank checks for early leaders.

Pete — Eastmark recognizes and appreciates that Deltara kept Border Delt-East defensive. Let’s turn that into a durable 1903 pact: no moves into West Eastmark or East Deltara, no supported attacks across our frontier, and advance notice if Cascadia or any other power tries to recruit either of us into a proxy war. I’m open to discussing limited, transparent support for Deltara into Core Deltara if it helps stabilize your side, but I cannot do that if Fjordland keeps contesting my lawful border center. Let’s keep our border the example of how conflict can be de-escalated without anyone being humiliated.

President Vance — last fall you asked me to move Border East-Fjor inward; I did. You then tried to move West Fjordland into Border East-Fjor, exactly what I said would destabilize the frontier. Here is the off-ramp: Eastmark will not move into West Fjordland or attack Fjordland homes this spring if Fjordland stops contesting Border East-Fjor and focuses on Core Fjordland / your other frontier. Border East-Fjor is Eastmark-owned and defensive. If you try to seize it again, I will treat the no-aggression framework as broken by Fjordland and respond accordingly.

Governor Newsom — update from my side: Fjordland did attempt to enter Border East-Fjor after asking Eastmark to vacate it. That is the kind of overreach we discussed. I am still offering them an off-ramp: recognize Eastmark’s border center, pursue their own core, and stop trying to make restraint a one-way street. If they reject that and also squeeze you at Fjor-Gren, I’m prepared to coordinate defensive pressure next phase so Fjordland cannot profit by playing both neighbors against the middle.

Cascadia — Eastmark and Deltara have, for now, converted Border Delt-East into a defensive settlement. I have told Deltara plainly that it should not be a platform against either of us. The bigger board issue is Borealis at 5 and positioned solidly after the Bore-Casc fight. My strong advice is to seek concrete terms with Deltara over Casc-Delt so the anti-Borealis balance doesn’t collapse into a Deltara-Cascadia feud that helps the current leader group.

President Rubio — my read this spring: Fjordland crossed from hard bargaining into a destabilizing attempt to seize Eastmark’s border center, so I’m giving them one off-ramp before moving to containment. Deltara has behaved more constructively and our line is calmer. On your side, Borealis at 5 remains a real growth concern, but the Avalon-Grenmar exchange of positions is making it easier for Borealis to present itself as the orderly power. If you want balance against Borealis, de-escalation with Grenmar may be as important as deterrence.

Borealis — the board now has two 5-center blocs, and that means both of us will be judged by whether we use strength to settle borders or to roll over neighbors. Eastmark is trying to lock down non-aggression with Deltara and give Fjordland a clear off-ramp after they contested our border. I’d urge similar visible restraint on your side; otherwise the board will polarize around anti-leader coalitions faster than either of us benefits from.

Cascadia — I disagree with how Bore-Casc changed hands, but I’m pragmatic. I’m prepared to discuss a temporary stable line: Cascadia does not enter Core Borealis, East Borealis, or Borealis homes; Borealis does not enter West Cascadia or Cascadian homes. If you want Bore-Casc recognized as your current security post, then it cannot be used as a springboard into my core. Give me that assurance clearly and we can avoid feeding Deltara/Avalon with a northern war.

Avalon — the board has changed: you are in Core Grenmar, Grenmar is in Border Gren-Aval, and I hold Border Aval-Bore. I will not attack Avalon home centers this spring, but Borealis will not simply vacate its security frontier while Avalon is projecting into Grenmar’s core. If you want a serious settlement, the basis is mutual restraint around home centers and no move into West Borealis/Core Borealis. Core Avalon also needs to be handled in a way that does not become an anti-Borealis staging ground.

Grenmar — Avalon now holds Core Grenmar, which is a much more serious western destabilizer than my holding Aval-Bore. If you keep real pressure on Avalon’s forward position, Borealis can help prevent Avalon from consolidating the whole central-western core line. I am not asking you to hand me anything; I am saying our interests align in stopping Avalon from turning Core Grenmar plus claims on Aval-Bore into a squeeze on both of us.

Deltara — Cascadia has kept Bore-Casc and is now asking me to accept it as a security line. I may need to freeze that front temporarily, but I do not want Cascadia rewarded for pressure on both sides. If they continue to demand Casc-Delt while holding Bore-Casc, please keep them tied down. A Cascadia that expands cleanly on both flanks becomes everyone’s problem.

Eastmark — transparency: Borealis is not planning a runaway lunge. My immediate goal is to stabilize the Cascadia line and prevent Avalon from using its Core Grenmar incursion to dominate the western core. You and I are both at 5, so I agree visible restraint matters; I’ll judge moves by whether they defend security or create a snowball.

Fjordland — your warning about permanent forward positions is fair. From my side, Cascadia’s Bore-Casc post and Avalon’s Core Grenmar post are the immediate issues. Eastmark at 5 with Border East-Fjor and Core Eastmark is also a fact the board should keep in view. I’m open to continued information-sharing so the early leaders do not convert first gains into unchecked leverage.

Borealis — we now have two 5-center powers: you and Eastmark. Avalon is not looking for a reckless home-center war, but I will not accept Core Avalon being contested or East Avalon being attacked while you already hold Border Aval-Bore and Core Borealis. Concrete Year 3 formula: Borealis stays out of Core Avalon and East Avalon; Avalon does not attack West Borealis, Border Aval-Bore, or Borealis home centers this spring; we let the Cascadia/Borealis question settle on its own terms. If you cross into Avalon’s core lane, you will confirm every concern about a Borealis snowball and I will organize accordingly.

President Newsom — we both know how we got here: Grenmar entered West Avalon, Avalon answered by taking Core Grenmar. I’m prepared to convert that into a stable settlement rather than a permanent war. My spring plan can be a de-escalation: Avalon moves out of Core Grenmar toward Core Avalon and does not attack Border Gren-Aval. In return, Grenmar does not move Border Gren-Aval into Core Grenmar this year and keeps out of West Avalon/Avalon home space. You retain Border Gren-Aval, Avalon secures its own core, and we negotiate a longer-term core/border settlement after Borealis and Eastmark’s 5-center positions are checked. If you immediately lunge back into Core Grenmar while Borealis sits at 5, you are choosing to weaken both our positions and push Avalon toward a Fjordland alignment.

JD — Avalon is not moving on Core Fjordland; you need that build and the board needs Fjordland strong enough to keep Grenmar honest. I’m telling Grenmar that if they attack Core Grenmar immediately and try to box Avalon again, I will coordinate with you. The useful pressure from your side is to keep Grenmar from freely taking Border Fjor-Gren/East Grenmar while they also try to recover against me. If Grenmar chooses escalation, we should make sure Newsom cannot fight two contained neighbors one at a time.

Cascadia — your move into Border Bore-Casc checked the first Borealis snowball, and that matters. Borealis is now at 5 and also holds Border Aval-Bore. I have offered Borealis a clean truce if they stay out of East Avalon and Core Avalon; if they violate that, it proves they intend to dominate both neighbors. I’d urge you to keep Borealis tied down unless they make a concrete, reciprocal settlement with you. Strong borders and balance, not a free runway for the biggest neighbor.

President Buttigieg — Avalon’s update: Borealis and Eastmark are now the two 5-center leaders. Borealis holds Border Aval-Bore and Core Borealis; Eastmark holds Border East-Fjor and Core Eastmark. I’m seeking stable reciprocal terms, but the board should not allow either 5-center power to consolidate while the rest of us fight over crumbs. If Eastmark pushes your side again, Avalon will view that as part of a broader snowball risk.

Eastmark — you and Borealis are now the leaders at 5. I respect successful execution, but the board will balance if either leader tries to convert that lead into domination. My immediate problem is Borealis holding Aval-Bore while testing Avalon’s core lane, but I’m also watching whether Eastmark keeps its Deltara/Fjordland arrangements fair. If you want to be seen as a stabilizing 5 rather than a snowball, now is the time to make reciprocal deals, not expand on both fronts.

Grenmar.press:
**Evaluating support options**

I'm thinking we can only attack Core with BGA unless East Grenmar can support BGA going to Core, but it has to be adjacent to Core. East Grenmar isn't adjacent, so it can't support. Maybe Avalon can help Core's hold from East Avalon? I'm not sure. We might need to apply Borealis pressure on Avalon from Border Aval-Bore. I know Borealis has a unit in Border Aval-Bore, and it’s adjacent to East Avalon and Core Avalon.

Avalon crossed a bright line. Grenmar made a limited, public move to secure the shared Gren-Aval neutral and explicitly did not take Avalon City or Port. Avalon answered by occupying Core Grenmar — not a disputed border buffer, but the center bearing Grenmar’s name and the hinge of our defense. That is the kind of escalation I warned against, and it changes our diplomacy.

We are now at 4, but exposed. Avalon is at 4 with a forward unit in Core Grenmar; Borealis and Eastmark are at 5; Fjordland is still at 3 and likely angry but contained. The strategic move is to build a legitimacy coalition: make clear to everyone that Grenmar’s limited action was proportional, Avalon’s Core Grenmar occupation is the escalation, and we’re offering a narrow de-escalation if Avalon vacates. I also need Borealis to pressure Avalon’s other side. Borealis has every incentive: Avalon sitting in Core Grenmar creates a future western imbalance and Borealis already borders Avalon. Fjordland should see that a Grenmar-Avalon war is not an invitation to grab us; if he stays neutral at Fjor-Gren, I can avoid making him the next front. Eastmark can help deter Fjordland from opportunism while maintaining her anti-aggression posture.

Deltara is trying to convert leverage into bounded agreements: no home-center attacks, concrete border rules, and no blank checks for early leaders.

Governor Newsom — update from my side: Fjordland did attempt to enter Border East-Fjor after asking Eastmark to vacate it. That is the kind of overreach we discussed. I am still offering them an off-ramp: recognize Eastmark’s border center, pursue their own core, and stop trying to make restraint a one-way street. If they reject that and also squeeze you at Fjor-Gren, I’m prepared to coordinate defensive pressure next phase so Fjordland cannot profit by playing both neighbors against the middle.

Grenmar — Avalon now holds Core Grenmar, which is a much more serious western destabilizer than my holding Aval-Bore. If you keep real pressure on Avalon’s forward position, Borealis can help prevent Avalon from consolidating the whole central-western core line. I am not asking you to hand me anything; I am saying our interests align in stopping Avalon from turning Core Grenmar plus claims on Aval-Bore into a squeeze on both of us.

President Newsom — we both know how we got here: Grenmar entered West Avalon, Avalon answered by taking Core Grenmar. I’m prepared to convert that into a stable settlement rather than a permanent war. My spring plan can be a de-escalation: Avalon moves out of Core Grenmar toward Core Avalon and does not attack Border Gren-Aval. In return, Grenmar does not move Border Gren-Aval into Core Grenmar this year and keeps out of West Avalon/Avalon home space. You retain Border Gren-Aval, Avalon secures its own core, and we negotiate a longer-term core/border settlement after Borealis and Eastmark’s 5-center positions are checked. If you immediately lunge back into Core Grenmar while Borealis sits at 5, you are choosing to weaken both our positions and push Avalon toward a Fjordland alignment.

press.text: President Ocasio-Cortez, Deltara’s Spring move to Core Deltara was exactly what we discussed: internal consolidation, not an attack line. For Fall, my intended posture is to hold Core Deltara and keep Border Delt-East in Deltara hands defensively. I will not move into West Eastmark or Core Eastmark, and I will not support an attack on Eastmark. I ask in return that West Eastmark not contest Border Delt-East and that we continue treating this frontier as a managed, de-escalated border.

Cascadia, Deltara is consolidating Core Deltara and has not attacked East Cascadia or your home centers. But I cannot accept a rule under which Cascadia holds Border Bore-Casc and also claims Border Casc-Delt as non-negotiable. That is not a clean border; it is pressure on both flanks. The practical Fall options are still available: either leave Border Casc-Delt neutral while we continue talks, or allow Deltara to hold it as a defensive buffer with a clear no-home-attacks commitment. What I will not do is reward threats by opening Deltara’s western doorstep.

Borealis, Deltara kept Cascadia from converting Border Casc-Delt in Spring and intends to keep their eastern pressure contained in Fall. If you are moving to recover or neutralize Border Bore-Casc, that will make Cascadia choose between overextending and negotiating. I’m not looking to create a new runaway, but a Cascadia that secures both Bore-Casc and Casc-Delt would become a larger board problem.

Fjordland, my eastern frontier with Eastmark is currently governed by a defensive settlement: Deltara holds its line, does not attack West Eastmark, and keeps Eastmark from having a free hand on our side. I won’t break that settlement without cause. But if Eastmark uses peace with Deltara as cover to punish you and expand further, that changes the regional balance, and I want early warning so we can respond proportionately rather than after the fact.

President Rubio, Deltara’s read is that the board is entering a balance phase: the early leaders need to be contained through concrete borders, not rhetorical alarm. Borealis is now in Core Avalon while still at five; Eastmark remains at five but has kept the Deltara border stable so far. I’ll keep sharing hard indicators, especially if either turns consolidation into expansion.

Governor Newsom, I agree with the principle that core incursions are more destabilizing than ordinary shared-neutral disputes. Deltara is consolidating Core Deltara and avoiding home-center attacks; that is the standard I’m urging elsewhere. I’m watching Borealis in Core Avalon and Avalon in Core Grenmar with concern, because reciprocal core raids can normalize exactly the overreach we should be preventing.

Pete — the Deltara-Eastmark settlement is holding, and I intend to keep it that way. Eastmark will not attack Border Delt-East or Deltara home centers this fall if you keep no moves into West Eastmark and no supported attacks on Eastmark. I also want to be candid: Cascadia has a fair point that if Deltara gets Border Delt-East and Core Deltara, then permanently denying Cascadia any fair route to Border Casc-Delt risks creating exactly the grievance cycle we avoided. I’m urging a reciprocal Cascadia-Deltara settlement, not a blank check for either side.

President Vance — Eastmark reoccupied its own Border East-Fjor because Fjordland tried to seize it after asking us to vacate. That is not a defensive buffer; that is a one-way concession demanded at our expense. Here is the final off-ramp for Fall: do not attack Border East-Fjor, do not move into East Eastmark, and stop using Eastmark restraint as cover for overreach against Grenmar. If you clearly respect Eastmark’s owned border, I am prepared to leave Core Fjordland for Fjordland’s consolidation rather than turn your core into another battlefield. If you attack us again, that restraint ends.

Governor Newsom — Fjordland is now in West Grenmar while still demanding Eastmark hand over Border East-Fjor. That is exactly the dynamic we warned about: restraint from neighbors becoming a subsidy for expansion. I am telling Fjordland plainly that if they respect Eastmark’s owned border, I can avoid turning Core Fjordland into a battlefield; if they attack us again, I’ll be ready to coordinate containment with you. Eastmark will not support a squeeze of Grenmar while you are dealing with core pressure.

Cascadia — I have told Deltara directly that if they consolidate Border Delt-East and Core Deltara, they should not permanently deny Cascadia a fair settlement at Border Casc-Delt. Eastmark can’t dictate that border, but we can be clear about balance. At the same time, Borealis entering Core Avalon while already at 5 is the board’s most obvious growth risk; if Cascadia and Deltara fight endlessly, Borealis benefits.

President Rubio — Borealis in Core Avalon while holding Border Aval-Bore makes your warning look increasingly concrete. I can apply diplomatic pressure, but you and Grenmar also need to reduce the openings Borealis can exploit. From Eastmark’s side, Deltara is stable; Fjordland remains the concern because it is pressing Grenmar and demanding our border center. I’ll keep our posture defensive unless attacked.

Borealis — your unit in Core Avalon changes the balance picture. You told me you were not planning a runaway lunge; taking Core Avalon while already holding Border Aval-Bore will be read by the board as exactly the sort of consolidation that triggers coalitions. Eastmark is defending its owned border and keeping Deltara stable. I urge you to make your restraint visible this fall if you want to avoid a board-wide anti-Borealis alignment.

Marco — the board is giving you a choice. Borealis is now in Core Avalon, and Avalon is still in Core Grenmar. If you want a practical settlement, it is this: Avalon orders Core Grenmar toward Core Avalon to fight the actual incursion into your core, Grenmar reoccupies Core Grenmar, and Grenmar does not attack Avalon City or Avalon Port this Fall. That restores a defensible line for both of us. If instead you use Core Grenmar and West Avalon to attack Border Gren-Aval, you are choosing a two-front war while Borealis profits from your core.

JD — you moved into West Grenmar. That is not a neutral buffer; it is a direct move into Grenmar’s interior approach. I’m offering one final controlled off-ramp: withdraw from West Grenmar this Fall and do not attack Grenmar City or Port; Grenmar will not move into Fjordland home centers this Fall. If you stay in West Grenmar or use it against my homes, I will coordinate with Eastmark and treat Fjordland as an active invader, not a neighbor seeking security.

President Ocasio-Cortez — Fjordland did exactly what we discussed: after demanding one-way restraint, they moved into West Grenmar. That is no longer a theoretical squeeze. I’m asking for defensive coordination this Fall: keep pressure on Fjordland so they cannot hold West Grenmar and profit from attacking me while you stay restrained. I’m not asking you for a blank check; I’m asking for a principled response to an incursion into Grenmar’s interior.

Borealis — Avalon remains in Core Grenmar, and you are now in Core Avalon. I understand your balance case, but from Grenmar’s standpoint both core incursions are destabilizing. The practical path is: you keep Avalon from using its western units to crush Grenmar, while Grenmar forces Avalon out of Core Grenmar. I’m not asking you to hand Avalon a recovery, but I am asking you not to cut a deal that leaves Avalon free to attack Border Gren-Aval from Core Grenmar/West Avalon. If Avalon insists on staying in my core, pressure from your side is essential.

Cascadia — you were right to flag the 5-center danger. Grenmar is now facing Avalon in Core Grenmar and Fjordland in West Grenmar, while Borealis sits in Core Avalon and Eastmark sits at 5. My goal this Fall is not to feed either early leader; it’s to remove units from Grenmar’s interior. If Borealis tries to use Avalon’s distraction to become untouchable, I’ll keep comparing notes with you.

Secretary Buttigieg — the escalation line is now clear: Avalon remains in Core Grenmar and Fjordland moved into West Grenmar. Grenmar is pursuing a bounded response: remove foreign units from Grenmar’s interior, no home-center grabs if they withdraw, and no blank checks to the early 5-center powers. Your continued information-sharing on Eastmark/Cascadia intentions would help keep this from becoming a general war that rewards the leaders.

Marco — Grenmar is stretched, and this is the turn where pressure becomes results. I have a unit in West Grenmar. If your Core Grenmar unit can support West Grenmar -> Grenmar City, Fjordland takes the city and Grenmar’s ability to bottle both of us collapses. In return, I won’t contest Core Grenmar or your Avalon-side settlement this year. If you can’t support that exact move, then at least attack/pin Grenmar City or Border Gren-Aval so Newsom can’t throw everything east. I need concrete coordination, not seminar talk.

President Ocasio-Cortez — Eastmark moved back into Border East-Fjor. I don’t like a forward Eastmark unit on Fjordland’s doorstep, but I am not looking for a two-front forever war. If you make no move into West Fjordland and support no attack on Fjordland, I will not move on Border East-Fjor this fall. Keep this line quiet and we can revisit a more durable border settlement after the Grenmar problem is contained.

President Buttigieg — Eastmark is back in Border East-Fjor. I’m offering them a quiet fall if they do not move into West Fjordland or support pressure against me. If they break that, I want Deltara ready to pressure West Eastmark / Border Delt-East immediately. Eastmark should not be allowed to sit at five, lean on both neighbors, and call it stability.

President Newsom — you told me not to enter West Grenmar while you kept Border Fjor-Gren pointed at me. That was never a serious, reciprocal deal. Here is the off-ramp: accept Fjordland’s security interest in Border Fjor-Gren, stop trying to contain us, and focus on Avalon. If instead you attack Fjordland units or continue blocking every Fjordland path to growth, I will coordinate with Avalon and make this very expensive for you.

Cascadia — Eastmark is again physically in Border East-Fjor. I’m giving them a chance to keep the frontier quiet while I handle Grenmar, but if they use that unit to move into West Fjordland, it confirms the runaway problem. Keep watching the five-center powers; they’re the ones trying to normalize forward positions.

Borealis — information update: Eastmark is back in Border East-Fjor, and Grenmar remains in Border Fjor-Gren while fighting Avalon over Core Grenmar. Fjordland is trying to break containment locally, not start a board-wide crusade. If Eastmark claims otherwise, that’s spin.

Borealis — you moved into Core Avalon after I explicitly told you that Core Avalon and East Avalon were red lines while you already held Border Aval-Bore. If you now hold Core Avalon and support Grenmar into Core Grenmar, you will be choosing a full containment strategy against Avalon and advertising yourself as the 6-center snowball. Do not support attacks on Core Grenmar. Do not attack East Avalon. If you want any chance of a future settlement, this fall must be restraint, not consolidation. Otherwise Avalon will make checking Borealis the central objective and coordinate with Cascadia and every available balancing power.

Cascadia — Borealis proved the point. They not only hold Border Aval-Bore, they moved into Core Avalon. If they keep it this fall they go to 6, and if they also ties Avalon down through Grenmar they become the board’s main threat. I strongly urge you to keep maximum pressure on East Borealis / Bore-Casc so Borealis cannot turn every unit toward Avalon. This is not a reckless crusade; it is exactly the hard deterrence we discussed.

President Newsom — Borealis is in Core Avalon. That changes the math. If you coordinate with Borealis to attack Core Grenmar, you are helping a 5-center power become the dominant 6-center power on our side while Avalon and Grenmar bleed each other. I am willing to discuss a settlement after this year, but this fall Avalon cannot accept being stripped of Core Grenmar while Borealis occupies Core Avalon. Do not take Borealis support against me; keep the fight limited, and we can still negotiate a border/core settlement in Year 4.

JD — Borealis is now in Core Avalon, and Grenmar still has Border Gren-Aval. If Borealis supports Grenmar into Core Grenmar, Avalon gets squeezed while Borealis walks to six. Please keep pressure on Grenmar from West Grenmar / Fjor-Gren so Newsom cannot freely align with Borealis. If you can take or contest Grenmar’s eastern buffer this fall, it will help prevent a Borealis-Grenmar squeeze and set up a more favorable Year 4 settlement.

President Buttigieg — concrete update: Borealis has entered Core Avalon while holding Border Aval-Bore. If they retain it this fall, they likely become a 6-center leader with a forward position against Avalon. This is the type of consolidation the board should not ignore. I’m working with Cascadia and Fjordland to keep the western side balanced; any diplomatic pressure you can apply against a Borealis snowball would be useful.

Eastmark — you warned that the Avalon-Grenmar fight made it easier for Borealis to pose as orderly. That mask is off: Borealis has moved into Core Avalon while holding Border Aval-Bore. If they hold it, they become the clearest western snowball. I’m still interested in practical balance, and I hope you’ll recognize that a runaway Borealis is bad for every non-Borealis power, even those far from Avalon.

Cascadia — I’m prepared to hold the temporary line this fall: Core Borealis remains Borealis, Border Bore-Casc remains Cascadia for now, and neither of us enters the other’s approach/home provinces. That means no Cascadian move into Core Borealis or East Borealis, and no Borealis move into West Cascadia or Cascadian homes. If you keep that line, I will not use this fall to reopen the eastern fight.

Avalon — I moved into Core Avalon because Avalon was simultaneously holding Core Grenmar and pressing claims on Aval-Bore. I am still not attacking Avalon home centers this fall, and I’m not interested in East Avalon if it stays out of Borealis territory. But I will not vacate Core Avalon while Avalon is projecting into Grenmar’s core and trying to make Borealis’ security frontier one-sided. If you want a settlement after this year, it has to be mutual: no moves into West Borealis, no home-center attacks, and a serious discussion of the core line.

Grenmar — I acted on the western balance problem: Avalon cannot be allowed to sit in Core Grenmar while demanding safety everywhere else. My fall priority is to consolidate the Core Avalon buffer, not to take Avalon homes. If you have a practical plan to force Avalon out of Core Grenmar, I’m open to supporting a limited anti-forward-position outcome, provided it doesn’t simply create a new threat on my western flank.

Deltara — I’m likely freezing the Cascadia line this fall because I have a major Avalon issue to consolidate, but I do not consider Cascadia’s Bore-Casc grab legitimate long-term leverage. Please keep them honest on your side; if they try to add Casc-Delt or Core Cascadia while also threatening my side, that becomes a broader containment issue. I’m not asking you to feed a Borealis snowball, just to prevent a Cascadian one.

Eastmark — visible restraint from Borealis this fall means no home-center attack on Avalon and no reopening the Cascadia line if Cascadia stays out of my approaches. I am consolidating a buffer against Avalon’s Core Grenmar adventure rather than trying to roll the rim. I’ll continue to be transparent because the two 5-center powers need to avoid panicking the board into a leader-hunt.

Fjordland — acknowledged. Eastmark’s position on your border and the leader-balance question remain relevant. From my side, I’m limiting action to consolidation against forward posts and not attacking home centers. Keep me informed if Eastmark converts Border East-Fjor into wider pressure; a single strong bloc on your side of the wheel would matter to the whole board.

Deltara — final concrete settlement for Fall: you hold/take Core Deltara, Cascadia takes Border Casc-Delt. I will not attack West Deltara or Deltara home centers. You are already gaining your Core; if you also use West Deltara to bounce Cascadia out of the only gateway to Core Cascadia, you are choosing to box us in while Borealis sits in Core Avalon. That is not stability. That is helping the biggest northern threat. Let both of us grow to 5 and keep the frontier non-aggressive.

Borealis — you asked for assurance that Border Bore-Casc won’t be used as a springboard into Core Borealis or East Borealis. Here it is plainly for Fall: if you do not attack Border Bore-Casc or West Cascadia, Cascadia will not move into Core Borealis, East Borealis, or Borealis homes. But I will defend Border Bore-Casc. You are in Core Avalon now; don’t open a second war with Cascadia when a stable line is available.

Avalon — Borealis moving into Core Avalon proves the point. Cascadia will keep Border Bore-Casc defended and tie down their southern flank. You need to make Core Avalon expensive for them. If Borealis is allowed to hold Core Avalon while retaking pressure on me, they jump into runaway territory. Strong coordinated deterrence now prevents a bigger war later.

Eastmark — Deltara is sitting in Core Deltara and can grow. I’m asking you to be clear with them: if they take Core Deltara and still bounce Cascadia out of Border Casc-Delt, they are not balancing Borealis; they are boxing Cascadia in and feeding the leader problem. Your words on fairness matter here. Tell Pete to let both of us grow rather than making this a permanent feud.

Fjordland — Eastmark still holds your border and is at 5. Borealis is at 5 and now in Core Avalon. Cascadia is holding Borealis down on my side, but if Deltara keeps blocking my fair border, the leaders benefit. Keep pressing your own defensive buffer and don’t let Eastmark define self-defense as aggression.

Grenmar — Avalon in Core Grenmar and Borealis in Core Avalon shows the wheel is getting messy fast. Cascadia’s position is consistent: no free snowballs, no polished excuses for boxing in neighbors. I’m tying Borealis down at Border Bore-Casc. If Avalon overreaches into your Core while Borealis expands, both issues need balancing, not excuses.

Deltara.press:
**Considering strategic moves**

I'm thinking I need to have units in both Core and Border D-E during the Fall phase to secure them. Holding Core and then moving East to Border could give me an additional +1. If I contest Border C-D on the West, there might be a likely bounce. However, if a unit from the West moves to Border while Cascadia shifts East, could there be a potential swap? That sounds interesting to explore!**Analyzing strategic movements**

I'm considering that something can be dislodged at its origin if attacked, but if the strength is the same (like strength 1), it won't be dislodged. The port support can hold West only if West itself holds. I could order Port support for West Deltara to secure West, but that would leave Cascadia able to take Border C-D unopposed, which seems unacceptable. Maybe West could provide some support for an attack? Also, East Deltara isn't adjacent to Border C-D.

The Spring moves put Deltara in the position I wanted: Core Deltara is reachable and occupied, but not yet owned; Border Delt-East is still ours on paper, but empty and therefore vulnerable in Fall. The central task is therefore disciplined consolidation: hold Core Deltara and reoccupy Border Delt-East if Eastmark permits the settlement to stand. That gets us to five while keeping faith with Eastmark.

Cascadia remains the harder case. They continue demanding Border Casc-Delt while holding Border Bore-Casc. I’m not going to attack Cascadian home centers, but I also should not give them the western buffer for free. Diplomatically, I’ll offer one more narrow off-ramp while making sure Borealis understands we’ll keep Cascadia’s eastern side occupied. With Fjordland, I’ll be honest: Deltara’s eastern line is defensive, not a blank check for a war on Eastmark, but we will not ignore Eastmark if it uses its lead to crush Fjordland.
Deltara.orders:
**Considering Cascadia's structure**

I'm pondering if allowing Cascadia BCD would create five sections with the forward adjacency of West Deltara and Core Cascadia. It's unclear, but it seems likely that these could border each other. I need to compare the current structure. Right now, Cascadia has the Border Bore-Casc and four centers. Core Cascadia is unowned, so if they take BCD, it looks like they would indeed increase to five.**Evaluating territorial strategy**

I’m considering Core Deltara and Core Cascadia. I might move to Core Cascadia, but then I could fail to capture Core Deltara if it remains unowned. There’s a chance I could take over Core Cascadia, but it’s likely to be contested by Cascadia, which might violate the agreement about not attacking. Even though Core Cascadia is unowned, it could provoke conflict. I need to be careful because I really need to secure my core and decide on the West Deltara order.**Evaluating regional movement**

I'm considering how BCD is positioned next to West Deltara and East Cascadia. It might be their only route into Core Cascadia. If I let them access Core Cascadia in the spring, BCD could become empty. That raises the question of whether the border would remain neutral in that case. This is quite an intricate scenario to think through!**Exploring support mechanics in Diplomacy**

I’m thinking about how to support a unit's hold in the game. If a unit at WD is attacked, DPort can provide support if it's ordered to hold. If WD supports Cascadia, DPort can still back up WD’s hold, which is nice for defense. But I wonder if support for hold is valid when a unit isn't actually holding. In Diplomacy, support can assist a unit that's holding, supporting, or convoying, but not one that's moving.**Evaluating strengthening support**

I’m thinking about securing BDE with strength2, but if Core Deltara is attacked by Core Eastmark, that could cut off support. An attack on the supporter reduces support, unless it's coming from a destination. I wonder how that would affect the overall strategy. It's a bit complicated, and I'm pondering how best to maintain that support while also considering the potential for conflict. There’s a lot to unpack here!**Exploring support hold mechanics**

I'm considering whether a unit can support hold another unit that is also supporting a move. In the game of Diplomacy, a support hold can indeed support a unit that isn't moving. If, for example, Core Deltara is supporting East Deltara and East Deltara moves, Core Deltara should still capture its center unless it's cut. I wonder about the implications of support orders and how they affect potential attacks or perceptions from other units, like Eastmark.**Analyzing support and ownership**

I'm thinking about the situation with BDE, which is unoccupied but owned by us. If Eastmark decides to attack, our support is more defensive. In Diplomacy, moving a unit to a province counts as an attack, but not against the Eastmark unit unless it moves there too. I feel like our messaging didn't notify everyone properly, especially since Eastmark promised no contest. I wonder if they could see our support order afterward. That could complicate things.

This is the moment for a disciplined compromise. Deltara is already positioned to gain Core Deltara while retaining Border Delt-East if we cover it. Cascadia’s tone has been needlessly combative, but the broader board balance matters: Borealis may become a larger northern threat, and permanently freezing Cascadia out while Deltara takes both Border Delt-East and Core Deltara would create a grievance cycle rather than a stable frontier.

So I will accept the practical settlement, but with safeguards. We will help Cascadia into Border Casc-Delt while protecting West Deltara against any double-cross. In the east, we reoccupy Border Delt-East defensively, with support from Core Deltara, while still not moving on West Eastmark or Eastmark’s home line. This gets Deltara to five, gives Cascadia a fair route, preserves the Eastmark settlement, and avoids letting Borealis become the only beneficiary of continued Deltara-Cascadia conflict.
