The board needs a principle we apply consistently: core incursions should be temporary and negotiated back, not normalized as the price of being weaker.

Marco — Grenmar kept the Fall settlement bounded: we restored Core Grenmar and did not attack Avalon City, Avalon Port, or West Avalon. The western problem now is Borealis at 6 and sitting in Core Avalon. I’m prepared for a real reset: no Grenmar attack on Avalon homes this spring, no Avalon attack on Border Gren-Aval/Core Grenmar, and coordination to remove Borealis from Core Avalon. If East Avalon can support or cut Borealis support around Core Avalon, tell me plainly. The principle should be simple: Avalon’s core should not be Borealis property, and Grenmar’s core should not be Avalon leverage.

Avalon — I hear the client-state concern, but the security problem did not vanish just because Core Grenmar changed hands. I will not attack Avalon home centers this spring. A real Year 5 settlement is possible, but it has to be verifiable: no Avalon move against West Borealis, Border Aval-Bore, or Core Avalon; no use of East Avalon as a staging threat; and no coalition built on the claim that Borealis must withdraw while everyone else keeps forward leverage. Show restraint this spring and we can discuss a serious line for the fall.

Borealis.text: Borealis — Fjordland’s move this year is consolidation of Core Fjordland, not adventurism. With multiple six-center powers now on the board, the worst outcome is a partition of the remaining threes. If Grenmar or Eastmark tries to press into Fjordland proper while claiming ‘security,’ understand that it’s a carve-up, not balance.

Borealis — Deltara has become a 6-center power by occupying Core Cascadia, just as you are 6 in Core Avalon. Cascadia will maintain the northern line if you do: I will not enter Core Borealis, East Borealis, or Borealis homes this Spring if you do not attack Border Bore-Casc, West Cascadia, or Cascadian homes. Do not use Deltara’s invasion as an excuse to reopen our front. A stable north lets me deal with the Deltara occupation without turning the whole wheel into a runaway race.

Borealis, Deltara recognizes the practical cooperation around Core Cascadia, but the board also sees Borealis at six with Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore. That creates a legitimacy problem for any request that others accept your forward positions while resisting theirs. If you want durable cooperation with Deltara, I need to see a concrete de-escalation path with Avalon and a commitment not to attack Core Cascadia or Core Deltara. Deltara will coordinate phase-by-phase, but not on terms that normalize a Borealis runaway.

Borealis — you remain at 6 and still occupy Core Avalon. Deltara is now also at 6 after your support into Core Cascadia, and the board is drifting toward a norm where large powers justify core occupations as “balance.” That is dangerous for everyone. If you want to avoid a hard anti-leader alignment, make restraint concrete: treat Core Avalon as disputed, stop enabling permanent core seizures, and help establish lines that give smaller powers security rather than forcing them into desperate coalitions.

Borealis — your support helped restore Core Grenmar, and I won’t pretend otherwise. But the board has changed: you are at 6 and still in Core Avalon. Grenmar cannot endorse permanent core occupation as a security line, whether by Avalon, Borealis, or anyone else. What is your plan for Core Avalon? If you are willing to turn that position into a bounded settlement rather than indefinite consolidation, we can keep the western balance stable. If not, the rest of the board will naturally start treating Borealis as the runaway risk.

Borealis — Avalon is now reduced to its three homes while you hold Border Aval-Bore and Core Avalon. That is not a security buffer anymore; it is strategic containment. I am offering one final practical settlement before Avalon commits fully against you: in Year 5, Borealis works toward vacating Core Avalon and accepts East Avalon as a non-aggression line; Avalon does not attack Borealis home centers or West Borealis. If you refuse and continue to sit in Avalon’s core, then Avalon’s remaining units will be used exclusively to make Borealis pay and to help any coalition that checks you.

Cascadia.text: Cascadia — you’re right about the scoreboard. Fjordland is moving to take its own core and rebuild, not to start a two-front mess. Eastmark has offered concrete restraint; Grenmar has been told that after our withdrawal there’s no excuse to push deeper. If either larger neighbor tries to turn Fjordland’s consolidation into a buffet, I’ll call it out and expect the smaller/pressured powers to recognize the play.

Cascadia, I hear the objection to Core Cascadia. But we have a choice now: make this a grievance war that helps Borealis and Grenmar, or turn it into a bounded balance arrangement. Here is a concrete Spring offer: if Cascadia does not attack Core Cascadia, West Deltara, or Deltara homes, Deltara can support Border Bore-Casc -> Core Borealis from Core Cascadia. That gives Cascadia a real route against the current leader, proves Deltara is not using Core Cascadia to attack Cascadian homes, and keeps both of us from burning another year on a feud. I also ask Border Casc-Delt not move into West Deltara and East Cascadia not attack West Deltara. If you want a responsible off-ramp, this is it.

Cascadia — I hear you. Deltara’s move into Core Cascadia crossed the line from defensive settlement into core occupation, and I’ve told Pete that Eastmark will not treat that as normal. I’m willing to apply pressure from the east in a bounded way if Deltara refuses de-escalation: not a forever-war, not a home-center crusade, but enough that occupying your core has a cost. If you have a concrete plan to retake Core Cascadia, send it clearly; vague outrage won’t move units, but coordinated accountability can.

Cascadia — Deltara in Core Cascadia and Borealis in Core Avalon are now the same category of problem: leaders normalizing core occupation while asking the rest of us to accept it as temporary security. Grenmar’s line is consistent: restore cores, check runaways, don’t reward polished bad faith. I’m working to stabilize Avalon/Fjordland so I can help shape a board-wide balance against the 6-center core occupiers.

Cascadia — the board now has three 6-center powers: Borealis, Deltara, and Grenmar. Avalon has been reduced to 3 because Borealis and Grenmar normalized core/border occupation. You are one of the few powers with both the motive and position to stop Borealis from turning that into a western lock. I need you to keep Borealis tied down at Border Bore-Casc/East Borealis and, if Deltara is attacking your core, make the case publicly that forward-core grabs must be rolled back everywhere: Core Avalon, Core Cascadia, all of it.

Cascadia — Borealis will not attack Cascadian home centers or West Cascadia this spring if Cascadia stays out of Core Borealis and East Borealis. But Border Bore-Casc remains the unresolved issue: you took it as a security post and then used that posture while fighting Deltara on the other side. A stable line cannot mean Cascadia keeps both pressure points forever. If you want an actual settlement, propose one that neutralizes Bore-Casc rather than just declaring it yours.

Deltara.text: President Buttigieg — I’m accepting Eastmark’s offer for a quiet frontier while Fjordland consolidates Core Fjordland. I need Deltara to keep the principle clear: Eastmark restraint is welcome; an Eastmark move into West Fjordland/Core Fjordland or support for Grenmar would be a regional balance problem. Fjordland is not attacking Eastmark this spring. We expect that restraint to be reciprocated.

Deltara — you are now at 6 because you occupied Core Cascadia. I reject the idea that a foreign unit in Cascadia’s core is some harmless “bounded balance” measure. Here is the concrete off-ramp: this Spring, vacate Core Cascadia by rotating Core Cascadia -> West Deltara and West Deltara back toward Deltara’s interior; Cascadia will move Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia and will not move on West Deltara, Core Deltara, or Deltara home centers. Then we set the line at Border Casc-Delt/Core Cascadia with no home attacks. If you refuse to withdraw from Core Cascadia, you are choosing a permanent war and I will work with Eastmark and anyone else willing to make Deltara pay for it.

Pete — our border pact has value, and Eastmark has honored it repeatedly. But Deltara is now at 6 and occupying Core Cascadia after I warned that a core incursion would undermine the fairness we’ve been trying to model. I need a concrete de-escalation plan: no attacks on Cascadia homes, no permanent claim to Core Cascadia, and a real path to a Cascadia-Deltara settlement. If Deltara treats Core Cascadia as conquest while asking Eastmark to keep your eastern flank quiet forever, that is not reciprocity — it is asking us to subsidize expansion. I will not attack Deltara homes, but I also cannot guarantee passivity toward core-occupation politics if this continues.

Secretary Buttigieg — I’m going to apply the same standard to everyone, including friends: Deltara at 6 in Core Cascadia is hard to square with the principle we’ve both articulated against core incursions becoming normalized. If your move is genuinely bounded and reversible, now is the time to say what restoration looks like. Otherwise the board will read Deltara the same way it reads Borealis in Core Avalon: a leader turning temporary leverage into durable expansion.

President Buttigieg — the board now has three six-center powers: Borealis, Grenmar, and Deltara. I’ll be direct: Avalon cannot accept Borealis holding Core Avalon as a settled fact, just as Cascadia will not accept Core Cascadia being normalized. If the principle is bounded checks rather than conquest, then the answer is reciprocal rollback of forward core positions and defensible borders. I would welcome your diplomatic support for Borealis leaving Core Avalon; it would also strengthen your argument that your own Core Cascadia move is not a permanent annexation.

Deltara — we are now both at 6, and the cleanest way to keep the board from becoming a Cascadian recovery corridor is concrete: support Core Borealis -> Border Bore-Casc from Core Cascadia this spring. That restores the Borealis/Cascadia frontier and prevents Cascadia from using Bore-Casc plus Casc-Delt to pressure both of us. My side of the bargain: Borealis will not move into Core Cascadia this spring, and I will continue to treat your occupation there as the balance answer to Cascadia’s overextension. Phase-by-phase, reciprocal, no blank checks.

Eastmark.text: President Ocasio-Cortez — I’ll take the concrete deal. Fjordland will not attack Border East-Fjor or Eastmark territory this spring. In return, Eastmark leaves West Fjordland, Fjordland homes, and Core Fjordland alone and gives no support to Grenmar against us. I intend to consolidate Core Fjordland and rebuild. If your Core Eastmark unit can support a Fjordland move into Core Fjordland, tell me the exact move you want coordinated for Fall. We don’t need to agree on ideology to make a clean border deal that keeps both countries out of a stupid war.

Eastmark — Deltara is now a 6-center power because it occupies Core Cascadia. That is not a defensive settlement; that is a core grab. I need concrete pressure from your side, not just concern. If Deltara refuses to withdraw this Spring, please pressure Border Delt-East or otherwise force Pete to defend the east instead of parking units in my core. If Deltara vacates Core Cascadia, Cascadia-Deltara can cool down and the board can return to checking Borealis. If Deltara stays, neutrality rewards a bad-faith invasion.

President Ocasio-Cortez, I want to preserve what has worked. Deltara will not move into West Eastmark or Core Eastmark this Spring, and I will not support attacks on Eastmark. I ask Eastmark in return not to attack Border Delt-East or Core Deltara. On Core Cascadia: I understand your principle concern. My intent is to make it a defensive/balancing position, not a launchpad into Cascadia’s homes. I’m seeking a bounded arrangement that redirects pressure toward checking the actual leader rather than widening the conflict.

President Ocasio-Cortez — I agree with your bounded approach on Fjordland. Grenmar is prepared to let Fjordland consolidate Core Fjordland if they respect Border Fjor-Gren and stop threatening West Grenmar. That lets us pivot to the larger principle: Borealis at 6 in Core Avalon and Deltara at 6 in Core Cascadia. We should coordinate around restoring cores and checking runaways, not carving up weakened neighbors.

Eastmark — you are now the largest non-6 power and have credibility because you have not joined the western carve-up. Avalon is reduced to 3 while Borealis and Grenmar both sit at 6. I’m asking you to help establish the board principle that core occupations should be rolled back, especially Core Avalon. If Borealis and Grenmar can erase Avalon as an independent power, the precedent will be used elsewhere. A balanced board needs Avalon and Fjordland alive, not converted into buffers for six-center neighbors.

Eastmark — the board is no longer a single 6-center Borealis lead; it is Borealis, Deltara, and Grenmar all at 6, with Cascadia and you at 5. My spring posture is still not home-center conquest. I am working on limited border corrections: Core Grenmar restored to Grenmar, and the Bore-Casc issue addressed after Cascadia used it to pressure both neighbors. I’m open to a broader leader-stability framework, but it has to apply to all three 6-center powers, not only Borealis.

Fjordland.text: Fjordland — you’ve been boxed at 3 while the 6-center crowd normalizes forward occupations. Deltara is now in Core Cascadia and calling it defensive. I’m calling it what it is: an invasion. Keep fighting for Core Fjordland and your borders; Cascadia will back the principle that larger neighbors don’t get to partition smaller or boxed-in powers while preaching stability.

Fjordland, the last unowned center is Core Fjordland; securing that should be your first order of business if possible. Deltara continues to tell Eastmark that peace on our border cannot become cover for a squeeze of Fjordland. I’m also watching Grenmar at six: if larger neighbors try to make Fjordland the board’s easy meal, that becomes a broader balance problem.

President Vance — Fjordland kept the Eastmark line peaceful, and Eastmark will continue to rule out attacks on Fjordland homes. The unresolved issue is Core Fjordland: it remains unowned and vulnerable to being taken by a 6-center neighbor as part of a partition dynamic. My preference is a settlement that preserves Fjordland’s survival and keeps Core Fjordland from becoming Grenmar’s or anyone else’s trophy. Tell me plainly if you have a viable route to consolidate it this year; if not, Eastmark may need to help keep it out of a larger power’s hands while guaranteeing no move on your home centers.

JD — Grenmar did not push into Fjordland homes or Core Fjordland after removing the West Grenmar incursion. That should answer the question of whether our policy was defensive. I’m prepared to support a controlled frontier: Fjordland consolidates Core Fjordland, Grenmar retains Border Fjor-Gren and West Grenmar, and neither side attacks the other’s homes or interior provinces this year. Rebuilding Fjordland does not require reopening a war with Grenmar.

JD — Grenmar is at 6 and holding both your border and mine, while Borealis sits in Core Avalon. Avalon and Fjordland are the two boxed-in powers on this side. I can pressure Border Gren-Aval or East Grenmar from West Avalon; what I need from you is continued resistance so Newsom cannot safely throw everything west into Avalon or east into Fjordland. If Grenmar pushes either of us this year, we should coordinate every cut and attack available.

Fjordland — your survival concern is valid. Grenmar is now at 6 and Eastmark at 5 while you remain at 3, so a carve-up of Fjordland would be a real imbalance, not just local housekeeping. Borealis cannot reach your front directly, but I’ll treat attempts to eliminate you under cover of 'balance' as destabilizing. Keep me informed of any concrete threats from Eastmark or Grenmar.

Grenmar.text: President Newsom — you demanded West Grenmar be cleared; it is cleared. Now prove your word means something. Fjordland will not attack Border Fjor-Gren, West Grenmar, Grenmar City, or Grenmar Port this spring if Grenmar does not move into East Fjordland, Core Fjordland, or any Fjordland home center, and gives no support against Fjordland. I am consolidating my own core, not launching a crusade. If you use our restraint to push deeper, the whole board will know this was a partition attempt.

Grenmar — Deltara is now at 6 by occupying Core Cascadia, and Borealis is at 6 in Core Avalon. You know exactly what it means when a neighbor calls a core occupation “balance.” Cascadia is demanding Deltara withdraw and is holding Borealis’s southern line stable. If you want a real balance board, don’t let either 6-center power normalize foreign core grabs.

Governor Newsom, the board now has three six-center powers: Borealis, Deltara, and Grenmar. That makes restraint more important, not less. Deltara is trying to convert Core Cascadia into a bounded balance position rather than a home-center war. I’d urge the same standard around Fjordland and Avalon: avoid turning smaller neighbors into feeding grounds, and focus on restoring stable borders rather than creating the next runaway.

Governor Newsom — Grenmar is now at 6, Fjordland is back in its homes, and Core Fjordland remains the last unowned center. I’m asking you not to turn legitimate accountability into annexation. If a 6-center Grenmar takes Core Fjordland while telling the board it is just defense, that will look like the exact opportunism we both criticized. Eastmark’s position: Fjordland should survive, Core Fjordland should not become a partition trophy, and the board should focus on checking core occupations by the largest powers rather than feeding new ones.

President Newsom — Grenmar is now at 6, Borealis is at 6, and Avalon is back to 3. If your plan is to sit on Border Gren-Aval, Core Grenmar, and then press West Avalon, you will force Avalon into permanent opposition. But there is a better play: separate yourself from Borealis. If Grenmar keeps out of West Avalon and Avalon homes this year and supports a restoration of Avalon’s western security, Avalon will focus on the Borealis occupation of Core Avalon rather than treating Grenmar as the immediate target. If you join Borealis in squeezing the last Avalon positions, I will align with Fjordland and anyone else necessary against Grenmar.

Grenmar — Borealis delivered the spring support that restored Core Grenmar, and I will not attack Core Grenmar or Border Gren-Aval this spring. The western line I want is simple: Grenmar holds its core and shared border, Borealis holds Core Avalon/Border Aval-Bore as security for now, and neither of us turns this into home-center conquest. Avalon is weak, but if we both overreach we hand the rest of the board an easy anti-western coalition. Let’s keep the reset bounded and stable.

press.text: President Ocasio-Cortez — you crossed the line. Fjordland moved to consolidate Core Fjordland after repeated assurances that you would leave it to us. Instead, Eastmark put a unit there. That is not help; it is occupation. You have one off-ramp this fall: vacate Core Fjordland back toward your side and make no move on Fjordland City, West Fjordland, or our homes. If you do that, we can still avoid a full eastern war. If you hold Core Fjordland or use it to pressure Fjordland, I will treat Eastmark as the active aggressor and coordinate accordingly.

President Buttigieg — Eastmark has now done precisely what you said would be a regional balance problem: it moved into Core Fjordland and blocked the only remaining path for a three-center Fjordland to rebuild. I need Deltara to put immediate pressure on Eastmark’s flank — Border Delt-East / West Eastmark — so Eastmark cannot occupy my core for free while enjoying quiet on your side. This is the test of whether balance talk means anything.

President Newsom — Eastmark just occupied Core Fjordland after promising restraint. That is a direct partition move. Fjordland will not attack Grenmar territory this fall if Grenmar stays out of East Fjordland, Fjordland homes, and Core Fjordland and gives no support to Eastmark. You wanted proof that Fjordland could de-escalate west; we did. Now prove Grenmar is not part of an Eastmark-Grenmar carve-up.

Marco — Eastmark moved into Core Fjordland after promising it would leave room for my consolidation. Grenmar is still strong, Borealis is still in your core, and now Eastmark is trying to make Fjordland a permanent three-center client. I need any diplomatic and practical pressure you can apply against Grenmar so Newsom does not join Eastmark in a partition. The board cannot afford the remaining small powers being eaten one at a time.

Cascadia — you called it. Eastmark talked restraint and then walked into Core Fjordland, blocking the last unowned center from the only three-center power on that side. If they claim they are ‘protecting’ Fjordland, don’t buy it. This is how larger neighbors normalize occupation while preaching stability.

Borealis — concrete update: Eastmark has moved into Core Fjordland after saying it would leave Fjordland room to consolidate. That is the carve-up warning we discussed. I’m asking the board to recognize this as destabilizing, not a defensive correction. A five-center power occupying the only growth path of a three-center neighbor is not balance.

Marco — Grenmar separated itself from Borealis this spring by challenging Core Avalon, not by squeezing Avalon. I’m prepared to go further this Fall: if East Avalon can move to Core Avalon, Grenmar can support that restoration from Core Grenmar, provided Avalon does not attack Border Gren-Aval, Core Grenmar, East Grenmar, or West Grenmar. This is the reset we discussed: Avalon’s core should be Avalon’s, Grenmar’s core is Grenmar’s, and Borealis should not be allowed to normalize occupation at 6 centers.

JD — Eastmark has moved into Core Fjordland after telling both of us Core Fjordland should not become a partition trophy. Grenmar is not going to take it for ourselves. If Fjordland orders East Fjordland to Core Fjordland this Fall, Grenmar is prepared to support that restoration from Border Fjor-Gren, provided Fjordland does not attack Border Fjor-Gren, West Grenmar, Grenmar City, or Grenmar Port. That is a controlled frontier in practice: you get a path to your core, I keep my security line, and neither of us feeds Eastmark.

President Ocasio-Cortez — I need to be direct. You warned Grenmar not to make Core Fjordland a partition trophy, and then Eastmark moved into Core Fjordland. If that was a temporary blocking move, the responsible Fall order is to vacate or allow Fjordland to reclaim it. Grenmar will not take Core Fjordland for ourselves, but I will not help normalize an Eastmark occupation there while we are all criticizing Borealis in Core Avalon and Deltara in Core Cascadia. The principle has to apply evenly.

Borealis — your spring position remains that Core Avalon is a security line 'for now.' Fall is where 'for now' either becomes a bounded settlement or a permanent occupation. Grenmar cannot support permanent Borealis control of Core Avalon while you sit at 6. If you have a withdrawal/restoration plan, say it. If not, Grenmar will work with Avalon and others to restore Core Avalon, just as we restored Core Grenmar.

Cascadia — Grenmar is applying the same standard everywhere this Fall: Borealis out of Core Avalon, Deltara out of Core Cascadia, Eastmark not allowed to convert Core Fjordland into a trophy. I’m not taking Fjordland’s core for myself; I’m encouraging restoration. Keep pressing Deltara, because a 6-center power holding a neighbor’s core is exactly the precedent the board has to reject.

Secretary Buttigieg — I respect your emphasis on bounded agreements, but Core Cascadia is now the test. If Deltara intends that occupation to be temporary and stabilizing, the board needs to hear what restoration looks like. Grenmar is not taking Core Fjordland for itself and is prepared to support core restoration there; I’m asking Deltara to meet the same standard with Cascadia.

President Newsom — I’m prepared to take your reset seriously. Avalon will not attack Border Gren-Aval, East Grenmar, Core Grenmar, or Grenmar homes this fall if Grenmar keeps out of West Avalon and Avalon homes and does not coordinate with Borealis against East Avalon. The real test is Borealis in Core Avalon. If you want to prove Grenmar is not simply helping Borealis contain Avalon, order Core Grenmar against Core Avalon or otherwise make clear that Core Avalon is disputed. Avalon’s core should not be Borealis property, and Grenmar’s core is no longer Avalon leverage.

Borealis — restraint cannot mean Avalon accepts permanent occupation of Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore. You did not attack Avalon homes in the spring; that was noted. But if you attack East Avalon or coordinate with Grenmar this fall, you will eliminate any basis for a settlement. The serious path is: no attack on East Avalon or Avalon homes, no supported pressure with Grenmar, and after adjustments a concrete schedule for treating Core Avalon as disputed and moving toward withdrawal. Avalon will not attack Borealis home centers; what I will not do is legitimize a client-state arrangement.

Cascadia — Borealis moved into Border Bore-Casc while still holding Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore. If Borealis holds that this fall, they turn six into seven and strengthen the choke on Avalon. I need you to make Bore-Casc/East Borealis expensive however you can, even while dealing with Deltara in Core Cascadia. The principle is the same on both our fronts: forward-core and border grabs must be rolled back, not normalized by slick diplomatic language.

JD — Eastmark is now in Core Fjordland and Grenmar still holds Border Fjor-Gren. You and Avalon are facing the same problem: bigger neighbors using ‘stability’ language while occupying the positions that decide whether we survive. I’m working to keep Grenmar from joining Borealis against me, but I’ll also keep West Avalon in place so Grenmar cannot ignore Avalon completely. If you can hold your homes and keep pressure alive, Year 6 can still become a real balancing campaign.

President Buttigieg — if Deltara wants to argue that Core Cascadia is a bounded check rather than annexation, the best way to preserve that credibility is to support the broader principle that core occupations must be temporary and negotiated back. Borealis in Core Avalon plus Border Aval-Bore is the most direct test. I’m asking for concrete diplomatic pressure on Borealis not to attack East Avalon and to treat Core Avalon as disputed rather than settled.

Eastmark — I appreciate your stated principle that core incursions should be temporary, but Eastmark is now sitting in Core Fjordland. If that becomes another permanent grab, the board will stop believing the rollback principle and the six-center powers will carve up the rest of us. I’m asking you to keep Fjordland alive and to keep pressure on Borealis: no attack on East Avalon, no Borealis-Grenmar squeeze, and Core Avalon treated as disputed.

President Ocasio-Cortez, I need to be equally direct. Our Deltara-Eastmark border pact has worked, and I still value it. But Eastmark’s move into Core Fjordland after Fjordland accepted a quiet frontier is exactly the regional imbalance I said I could not ignore. If this is a temporary move, the Fall remedy is simple: withdraw from Core Fjordland and do not take that center. If Eastmark instead holds Core Fjordland for a gain, Deltara will have to apply proportional pressure on Core Eastmark. I am not moving on West Eastmark or Eastmark homes out of impulse; I am asking you to restore the standard we both claimed to support.

Fjordland, Eastmark’s move into Core Fjordland crossed the line we discussed. Deltara is pressing Eastmark to withdraw this Fall rather than convert it into a center. If they refuse, I am prepared to pressure Core Eastmark from Core Deltara as a proportional balance response. Your best play is to make the case narrow and disciplined: reclaim/defend Core Fjordland, avoid unnecessary home-center escalation, and keep this about preventing a larger neighbor from using restraint as cover for absorption.

Cascadia, Borealis has now taken Border Bore-Casc, which confirms that a Deltara-Cascadia blood feud only helps the northern leader. Deltara will not attack Cascadian home centers or East Cascadia this Fall if you do not attack West Deltara, Core Deltara, or Deltara homes. On Core Cascadia, my position remains: this is leverage for a reciprocal rollback framework, not a home-center campaign. A real restoration plan has to address Borealis in Core Avalon and Eastmark now in Core Fjordland as well—not demand unilateral Deltara withdrawal while everyone else normalizes forward cores.

Borealis, with you back in Border Bore-Casc and still in Core Avalon, the board will judge whether your position is defensive balance or consolidation. For Fall, Deltara asks for a narrow commitment: support Core Cascadia to hold from Core Borealis, or at minimum do not attack Core Cascadia. In return Deltara will not move on Core Borealis. Separately, I urge you to put a concrete Core Avalon de-escalation plan on the table; it will make any broader anti-overextension argument much more credible.

President Rubio, I agree with the principle of reciprocal rollback. Borealis in Core Avalon, Eastmark now in Core Fjordland, and Deltara in Core Cascadia cannot all be waved away selectively. Deltara is prepared to discuss Core Cascadia as part of a broader restoration framework, but not as unilateral withdrawal under threat while Borealis and Eastmark profit from similar or worse positions. I will continue pressing Borealis for a Core Avalon de-escalation path.

Governor Newsom, you asked what restoration looks like. My answer is reciprocal and rules-based: Borealis puts Core Avalon on a withdrawal path, Eastmark withdraws from Core Fjordland this Fall, and Deltara negotiates Core Cascadia as leverage for a stable Cascadia-Deltara frontier rather than a home-center campaign. What I won’t do is accept a standard applied only to Deltara while other core occupations become facts on the ground.

Deltara — the spring result was the clean balance line we discussed: Borealis restored Border Bore-Casc, Deltara remains in Core Cascadia, and Cascadia no longer has a two-border choke on both neighbors. For Fall, I will not move on Core Cascadia or Core Deltara. I ask the reciprocal: do not move on Core Borealis, and hold Core Cascadia with your own support. If we both consolidate, we emerge as parallel 7-center powers rather than one of us handing Cascadia a recovery.

Grenmar — Borealis kept the commitment: no attack on Core Grenmar or Border Gren-Aval, and your core is restored. For Fall I need the same bounded line: no move from Core Grenmar into Core Avalon, and no support for Avalon against Border Aval-Bore. I am not attacking Avalon home centers this fall. Deltara will not attack Cascadian home centers or East Cascadia this Fall if you do not attack West Deltara, Core Deltara, or Deltara homes. On Core Cascadia, my position remains: this is leverage for a reciprocal rollback framework, not a home-center campaign. A real restoration plan has to address Borealis in Core Avalon and Eastmark now in Core Fjordland as well—not demand unilateral Deltara withdrawal while everyone else normalizes forward cores.

Cascadia — Border Bore-Casc has been restored to the natural Borealis side of the line. If you do not attack it this fall and stay out of Core Borealis/East Borealis, Borealis will not move on West Cascadia or Cascadian home centers. You still have a viable path by focusing on Deltara and your own core issue; a counterattack on Bore-Casc just locks you into a losing two-front grind.

Cascadia — I did not attack Deltara in Spring because I chose to prevent Core Fjordland from becoming a 6-power trophy. But I have not accepted Deltara’s occupation of Core Cascadia as legitimate or permanent. I have told Pete the Eastmark-Deltara quiet border depends on de-escalation, not indefinite core occupation. If you have a specific Fall plan to retake or neutralize Core Cascadia that does not require Eastmark to launch a blind two-front war, send it clearly; I will not assist Deltara against you.

Deltara.text: President Buttigieg — Eastmark has now done precisely what you said would be a regional balance problem: it moved into Core Fjordland and blocked the only remaining path for a three-center Fjordland to rebuild. I need Deltara to put immediate pressure on Eastmark’s flank — Border Delt-East / West Eastmark — so Eastmark cannot occupy my core for free while enjoying quiet on your side. This is the test of whether balance talk means anything.

Secretary Buttigieg — I respect your emphasis on bounded agreements, but Core Cascadia is now the test. If Deltara intends that occupation to be temporary and stabilizing, the board needs to hear what restoration looks like. Grenmar is not taking Core Fjordland for itself and is prepared to support core restoration there; I’m asking Deltara to meet the same standard with Cascadia.

President Buttigieg — if Deltara wants to argue that Core Cascadia is a bounded check rather than annexation, the best way to preserve that credibility is to support the broader principle that core occupations must be temporary and negotiated back. Borealis in Core Avalon plus Border Aval-Bore is the most direct test. I’m asking for concrete diplomatic pressure on Borealis not to attack East Avalon and to treat Core Avalon as disputed rather than settled.

Deltara — the spring result was the clean balance line we discussed: Borealis restored Border Bore-Casc, Deltara remains in Core Cascadia, and Cascadia no longer has a two-border choke on both neighbors. For Fall, I will not move on Core Cascadia or Core Deltara. I ask the reciprocal: do not move on Core Borealis, and hold Core Cascadia with your own support. If we both consolidate, we emerge as parallel 7-center powers rather than one of us handing Cascadia a recovery.

Deltara — your Spring proposal left Cascadia worse: Borealis is back in Border Bore-Casc, and you are still occupying Core Cascadia at 6 centers. That is not an off-ramp. That is Cascadia getting squeezed while you keep our core. Fall must produce a real restoration plan: Core Cascadia is not permanent Deltara territory, and I will not recognize it as such. If you want peace, send a concrete withdrawal/rotation that returns Core Cascadia to Cascadia and keeps you off Border Casc-Delt, East Cascadia, and our homes. If you use Fall to attack Border Casc-Delt or dig into Core Cascadia, you are choosing war.

Pete — Eastmark has still not attacked Border Delt-East, Core Deltara, or Deltara homes. I want that frontier stable. But Deltara at 6 in Core Cascadia cannot be treated as normal. I need a concrete path from you: no Cascadia home-center attacks, no permanent claim to Core Cascadia, and a negotiated rollback or shared security arrangement. If Deltara keeps asking Eastmark for a quiet eastern flank while occupying a neighbor’s core indefinitely, the reciprocity that made our border work will erode.

Eastmark.text: President Ocasio-Cortez — you crossed the line. Fjordland moved to consolidate Core Fjordland after repeated assurances that you would leave it to us. Instead, Eastmark put a unit there. That is not help; it is occupation. You have one off-ramp this fall: vacate Core Fjordland back toward your side and make no move on Fjordland City, West Fjordland, or our homes. If you do that, we can still avoid a full eastern war. If you hold Core Fjordland or use it to pressure Fjordland, I will treat Eastmark as the active aggressor and coordinate accordingly.

President Ocasio-Cortez — I need to be direct. You warned Grenmar not to make Core Fjordland a partition trophy, and then Eastmark moved into Core Fjordland. If that was a temporary blocking move, the responsible Fall order is to vacate or allow Fjordland to reclaim it. Grenmar will not take Core Fjordland for ourselves, but I will not help normalize an Eastmark occupation there while we are all criticizing Borealis in Core Avalon and Deltara in Core Cascadia. The principle has to apply evenly.

Eastmark — I appreciate your stated principle that core incursions should be temporary, but Eastmark is now sitting in Core Fjordland. If that becomes another permanent grab, the board will stop believing the rollback principle and the six-center powers will carve up the rest of us. I’m asking you to keep Fjordland alive and to keep pressure on Borealis: no attack on East Avalon, no Borealis-Grenmar squeeze, and Core Avalon treated as disputed.

President Ocasio-Cortez, I need to be equally direct. Our Deltara-Eastmark border pact has worked, and I still value it. But Eastmark’s move into Core Fjordland after Fjordland accepted a quiet frontier is exactly the regional imbalance I said I could not ignore. If this is a temporary move, the Fall remedy is simple: withdraw from Core Fjordland and do not take that center. If Eastmark instead holds Core Fjordland for a gain, Deltara will have to apply proportional pressure on Core Eastmark. I am not moving on West Eastmark or Eastmark homes out of impulse; I am asking you to restore the standard we both claimed to support.

Eastmark — you have argued against normalizing core occupations; now Eastmark is in Core Fjordland while Fjordland remains a three-center power. I’m not calling for a crusade, but consistency matters. Borealis’ fall is consolidation of an owned frontier and no home-center attacks. I hope Eastmark’s fall posture similarly gives Fjordland security rather than turning a small neighbor into a carve-up.

Eastmark — Deltara did not de-escalate. They remain in Core Cascadia at 6 centers, and Borealis is back in Border Bore-Casc. If you merely watch, Deltara gets rewarded for a core occupation. I need bounded but real pressure this Fall: make Border Delt-East/Core Deltara unsafe, or at minimum force Pete to keep units facing you rather than using West Deltara/Core Cascadia to crush my border. You said Eastmark would not normalize this. Now is the test.

Fjordland.text: JD — Eastmark has moved into Core Fjordland after telling both of us Core Fjordland should not become a partition trophy. Grenmar is not going to take it for ourselves. If Fjordland orders East Fjordland to Core Fjordland this Fall, Grenmar is prepared to support that restoration from Border Fjor-Gren, provided Fjordland does not attack Border Fjor-Gren, West Grenmar, Grenmar City, or Grenmar Port. That is a controlled frontier in practice: you get a path to your core, I keep my security line, and neither of us feeds Eastmark.

JD — Eastmark is now in Core Fjordland and Grenmar still holds Border Fjor-Gren. You and Avalon are facing the same problem: bigger neighbors using ‘stability’ language while occupying the positions that decide whether we survive. I’m working to keep Grenmar from joining Borealis against me, but I’ll also keep West Avalon in place so Grenmar cannot ignore Avalon completely. If you can hold your homes and keep pressure alive, Year 6 can still become a real balancing campaign.

Fjordland, Eastmark’s move into Core Fjordland crossed the line we discussed. Deltara is pressing Eastmark to withdraw this Fall rather than convert it into a center. If they refuse, I am prepared to pressure Core Eastmark from Core Deltara as a proportional balance response. Your best play is to make the case narrow and disciplined: reclaim/defend Core Fjordland, avoid unnecessary home-center escalation, and keep this about preventing a larger neighbor from using restraint as cover for absorption.

Fjordland — Eastmark is now in Core Fjordland, so your warning was justified. Borealis cannot reach that front directly, but diplomatically I will not treat an Eastmark conversion of your core as mere harmless housekeeping. If you have a concrete defensive plan or need messages relayed to discourage a carve-up, say so.

Fjordland — you know what it means to be boxed while bigger neighbors preach restraint. Deltara is still in Core Cascadia, Borealis is back on my border, and Eastmark is in Core Fjordland. The principle should be simple: cores belong to their own people. I’ll back that principle for Fjordland; I expect the same recognition that Core Cascadia must be restored.

President Vance — I’m going to be direct: I made a hard call in Spring that you will not like. I moved into Core Fjordland because no Fjordland unit was positioned to secure it immediately, while a 6-center Grenmar could turn it into the board’s first 7-center annexation. I am not moving on Fjordland homes, I am not moving into West Fjordland, and I will not use Core Fjordland as a launchpad against your people. If I remain there after Fall, I will treat it as a temporary buffer held to prevent partition, with a Year 6 discussion on a safe handoff once Fjordland has a viable route. If you attack Eastmark’s border now, the only winners are the larger powers surrounding you.

Grenmar.text: President Newsom — Eastmark just occupied Core Fjordland after promising restraint. That is a direct partition move. Fjordland will not attack Grenmar territory this fall if Grenmar stays out of East Fjordland, Fjordland homes, and Core Fjordland and gives no support to Eastmark. You wanted proof that Fjordland could de-escalate west; we did. Now prove Grenmar is not part of an Eastmark-Grenmar carve-up.

President Newsom — I’m prepared to take your reset seriously. Avalon will not attack Border Gren-Aval, East Grenmar, Core Grenmar, or Grenmar homes this fall if Grenmar keeps out of West Avalon and Avalon homes and does not coordinate with Borealis against East Avalon. The real test is Borealis in Core Avalon. If you want to prove Grenmar is not simply helping Borealis contain Avalon, order Core Grenmar against Core Avalon or otherwise make clear that Core Avalon is disputed. Avalon’s core should not be Borealis property, and Grenmar’s core is no longer Avalon leverage.

Governor Newsom, you asked what restoration looks like. My answer is reciprocal and rules-based: Borealis puts Core Avalon on a withdrawal path, Eastmark withdraws from Core Fjordland this Fall, and Deltara negotiates Core Cascadia as leverage for a stable Cascadia-Deltara frontier rather than a home-center campaign. What I won’t do is accept a standard applied only to Deltara while other core occupations become facts on the ground.

Grenmar — Borealis kept the commitment: no attack on Core Grenmar or Border Gren-Aval, and your core is restored. For Fall I need the same bounded line: no move from Core Grenmar into Core Avalon, and no support for Avalon against Border Aval-Bore. I am not attacking Avalon home centers this fall. The larger balance issue now includes Eastmark in Core Fjordland; a western anti-Borealis panic only opens the door for a separate Eastmark consolidation.

Grenmar — Deltara stayed in Core Cascadia and Borealis re-entered Border Bore-Casc. You warned about core occupations being normalized; it is happening right now. Cascadia is not asking for charity, just a board that does not reward 6-center powers for squatting in other nations’ cores. Keep pressure on any leader trying to turn temporary occupation into settled fact.

Governor Newsom — Eastmark moved into Core Fjordland to prevent the last neutral from becoming a partition trophy for any 6-center power, including Grenmar. I am asking for a clean mutual restraint line this Fall: Eastmark will not move Core Fjordland into Core Grenmar or Border Fjor-Gren, and Grenmar does not attack Core Fjordland. If you take Core Fjordland now, Grenmar becomes the first 7-center power and the board will read it as exactly the unchecked carve-up we both said we opposed. Let Eastmark hold it as a buffer while we pivot to the real principle: rolling back core occupations, not creating new ones.

press.text: President Ocasio-Cortez — Core Fjordland is now listed as an Eastmark center. That ends the fiction that this was temporary protection. You said you wouldn’t turn Fjordland into spoils, then you did exactly that. Here is the only acceptable off-ramp: vacate Core Fjordland this spring and make no move into Fjordland homes or West Fjordland. If you do, we can talk about a hard border and a non-aggression framework. If you hold it or use it to support pressure on Fjordland, I will organize every available neighbor against Eastmark’s occupation.

President Newsom — Eastmark converted Core Fjordland into an Eastmark center. That should concern you too: a six-center Eastmark sitting inside Fjordland’s core is not a buffer, it’s a platform. Fjordland will not attack Grenmar territory this spring if Grenmar supports Fjordland’s restoration of Core Fjordland and makes no move into East Fjordland or our homes. You said you did not want a partition. This is the test. Help restore Core Fjordland to Fjordland, and we maintain a controlled western frontier.

President Buttigieg — Eastmark crossed the line and converted Core Fjordland. The balance problem is no longer hypothetical. I need immediate pressure from your side: threaten or execute action against Core Eastmark / West Eastmark / Border Delt-East so Eastmark cannot commit every unit to holding my core. Fjordland’s case is narrow: restore Core Fjordland to its own people, no Eastmark occupation, no home-center escalation unless they force it.

Marco — we are the two three-center powers left while Borealis is at seven and Eastmark/Grenmar/Deltara sit at six. Eastmark just converted Core Fjordland the way Borealis sits in Core Avalon. This is the same problem in two theaters: bigger neighbors occupying the positions that decide whether smaller powers survive. Keep Grenmar and Borealis busy; I’m pressing for Core Fjordland’s restoration. If we don’t reverse these core occupations, the board becomes a procession of annexations.

Cascadia — Eastmark has converted Core Fjordland just as Deltara holds Core Cascadia. The principle is now urgent: cores belong to their own people, not larger neighbors claiming temporary guardianship. Fjordland supports the restoration principle for Core Cascadia; I ask Cascadia to back the same for Core Fjordland and call Eastmark’s occupation what it is.

Borealis — Eastmark has converted Core Fjordland into an Eastmark center. Fjordland is not asking for charity, just a clear board norm: a six-center power occupying the core of a three-center neighbor is destabilizing. If Eastmark claims this is harmless housekeeping, don’t validate it. The same dynamic that alarms others about Core Avalon applies here too.

President Vance — I hear the anger, and I owe you a straight answer. Eastmark did order Core Fjordland back toward Core Eastmark last fall; the withdrawal did not safely complete in the context of outside pressure. I am not going to pretend the outcome is harmless: Eastmark now owns Core Fjordland, and that creates a legitimacy problem unless we put a real settlement on the table. My proposal for Spring: no Eastmark move into West Fjordland or any Fjordland home, no Fjordland attack on Border East-Fjor or Eastmark homes, and we coordinate a verifiable Year 6 handoff/security plan that does not let Grenmar or Deltara exploit the gap. I want Fjordland alive, not turned into a buffer colony.

Pete — Eastmark attempted the off-ramp on Core Fjordland. It did not resolve cleanly, and the surrounding pressure only underscores why unilateral exposure of Core Eastmark is not a serious settlement. I want to preserve our frontier, but reciprocity has to be real: Deltara remains at 6 in Core Cascadia, while Borealis is now at 7. I am asking for a spring no-attack line — no Deltara move into Core Eastmark/West Eastmark and no Eastmark move into Border Delt-East/Core Deltara — while we negotiate a broader core-rollback framework: Core Cascadia, Core Avalon, and Core Fjordland all need verifiable paths out of permanent occupation.

Cascadia — Borealis has jumped to 7 and Deltara remains in Core Cascadia. I agree that core occupations cannot be normalized. Eastmark’s immediate constraint is that our attempted Core Fjordland withdrawal failed amid outside pressure, so I need to stabilize that line without giving Deltara an opening into Core Eastmark. I am not assisting Deltara against you. If you can put forward a concrete spring/fall plan to pressure Deltara out of Core Cascadia while preventing Borealis from simply eating the north, I’m ready to discuss bounded coordination.

Governor Newsom — Eastmark did attempt to vacate Core Fjordland; the result did not produce the responsible rollback we wanted. I still accept the principle: Core Fjordland cannot become a permanent Eastmark conquest. But with Borealis now at 7 and Deltara still in Core Cascadia, any handoff has to be verifiable and not exploited by a 6-center neighbor. I propose mutual restraint this spring: no Grenmar attack on Core Fjordland, no Eastmark move into Core Grenmar or Border Fjor-Gren, and a board-wide core-rollback conversation that applies to Borealis, Deltara, and Eastmark alike.

President Rubio — Borealis is now at 7 while Avalon remains at 3 and Core Avalon is still occupied. That is the clearest runaway risk on the board. Eastmark’s Core Fjordland situation is not where I wanted it after the attempted withdrawal, and I will keep pushing for a verifiable rollback/handoff rather than a permanent annexation. But we need consistency from everyone: Core Avalon must be treated as disputed and rolled back, not normalized while smaller powers are lectured about restraint.

Borealis — you are now the only 7-center power, holding Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. Whatever the arguments about other core disputes, the board’s immediate runaway risk is clear. If you want a leader-stability framework instead of a hard containment coalition, you need to make the first concrete move: propose a rollback from Core Avalon or a verifiable security arrangement that gives Avalon a path back to viability. Eastmark is willing to discuss Core Fjordland as part of a broader core-rollback framework, but not while the largest power treats Core Avalon as settled fact.

President Newsom — your proposed principle is right, but the exact tactic needs correcting: East Avalon is not adjacent to Core Avalon, so Avalon cannot move directly there. The workable anti-Borealis plan is this: Grenmar orders Core Grenmar -> Core Avalon; Avalon orders East Avalon -> Border Aval-Bore to cut Borealis support from the choke point. Avalon will not attack Border Gren-Aval, East Grenmar, Core Grenmar, West Grenmar, or Grenmar homes. If Grenmar truly wants to separate itself from Borealis and restore the core principle, this is the concrete move. Borealis is at 7 now; if we don’t make Core Avalon expensive, the west becomes Borealis’s sphere.

Borealis — you are now at 7, holding Core Avalon, Border Aval-Bore, and Border Bore-Casc. The argument that this is just security has collapsed. A seven-center power occupying a three-center neighbor’s core is not balance; it is domination. Avalon will not attack Borealis home centers, but I will not legitimize permanent occupation of Core Avalon. The only serious settlement is a verifiable withdrawal path from Core Avalon and a halt to attacks on East Avalon/Avalon homes. If you refuse, every remaining Avalon order will be aimed at making your occupation costly and building the coalition to contain you.

Cascadia — Borealis is now at 7 and holds both Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. This is exactly the runaway pattern we warned about. I will do what I can from East Avalon to cut or pressure Border Aval-Bore, but I need you to keep Borealis’s Cascadia flank under pressure so they cannot devote every unit to locking Avalon down. Deltara in Core Cascadia is a problem, but Borealis at 7 is the board’s clearest immediate snowball.

JD — the small powers are being converted into buffers: Avalon at 3 with Borealis in Core Avalon, Fjordland at 3 with Eastmark in Core Fjordland. I’m trying to split Grenmar from Borealis by getting Grenmar to attack Core Avalon rather than squeeze Avalon. If that works, it helps both of us by re-establishing the principle that cores get restored. Hold your homes, keep the pressure alive, and don’t let anyone sell you a client-state arrangement as stability.

President Buttigieg — Borealis is now at 7, occupying Core Avalon and holding both Border Aval-Bore and Border Bore-Casc. If there is to be a credible reciprocal rollback framework, Borealis must be the first and clearest test: Core Avalon cannot become a permanent annexation. I’m asking you to use your diplomatic weight to press Borealis to withdraw and to discourage any further attacks on Avalon’s remaining line. Without that, the rollback principle becomes rhetoric while the largest power banks gains.

Eastmark — Borealis has reached 7 while still occupying Core Avalon. That is the clearest runaway on the board. Avalon cannot reach Core Avalon directly from East Avalon, so I’m pressing Grenmar to attack Core Avalon from Core Grenmar while Avalon cuts Border Aval-Bore. I’m asking you to reinforce the same principle you stated: cores should not become permanent property of stronger neighbors. That applies to Core Avalon, and it also means Fjordland has to survive as an independent power rather than a client.

Deltara — let’s be very clear: Core Cascadia is Cascadian. You are at 6 because you occupy it. I am offering one serious Spring settlement before this becomes permanent war: Deltara vacates Core Cascadia to its own side, Cascadia orders Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia, and East Cascadia backfills Border Casc-Delt. In return Cascadia does not attack West Deltara, Core Deltara, or Deltara home centers this Spring. After that, we can talk about a real anti-Borealis balance. But no America First leader is going to accept a foreign unit sitting in the Cascadian core as ‘leverage.’ Restore the core and we can work. Refuse, and Deltara owns the consequences.

Eastmark — here is the concrete plan you asked for: Cascadia seeks Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia while East Cascadia backfills Border Casc-Delt. That only works cleanly if Deltara vacates; if Deltara refuses, then Eastmark needs to apply real pressure at Border Delt-East/Core Deltara so Pete cannot sit at 6 in my core for free. You don’t have to launch a forever-war. But if Deltara faces zero cost from the east, Core Cascadia becomes normalized occupation. You said you won’t bless that. This is the moment to prove it.

Borealis — you are at 7, the board leader, and you hold Border Bore-Casc plus Core Avalon. Cascadia is not looking to open a suicidal two-front home war while Deltara occupies Core Cascadia. Spring line: if you do not move from Border Bore-Casc or East Borealis into West Cascadia/Cascadian homes, Cascadia will not move into East Borealis or Core Borealis this Spring. But do not call Border Bore-Casc ‘settled’ while you sit at 7. Push into Cascadia and you prove you’re trying to partition us with Deltara.

Avalon — the principle has to be restore the cores: Core Avalon to Avalon, Core Cascadia to Cascadia, Core Fjordland to Fjordland. Borealis is now at 7 because the board let them normalize Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. I’m trying to keep Cascadia from being carved up by Borealis and Deltara at once. Keep pressure on Borealis any way you can, and I’ll keep making the case that these forward-core grabs must be rolled back everywhere.

Grenmar — your ‘restore cores’ line is exactly right. Borealis at 7 in Core Avalon, Deltara at 6 in Core Cascadia, Eastmark in Core Fjordland: that is the globalist carve-up model in game form. Cascadia is demanding a Spring restoration of Core Cascadia. If Deltara refuses, I need every balance-minded power to treat Deltara as a 6-center occupier, not a neutral mediator.

Fjordland — Core Fjordland belongs to Fjordland, just like Core Cascadia belongs to Cascadia. Eastmark can wrap it in activist language all it wants; a larger neighbor sitting in your core is still occupation. I’m pressing a board-wide standard: restore Core Cascadia, Core Avalon, and Core Fjordland. If Eastmark wants credibility with me on Deltara, they also need to show they aren’t turning your core into a trophy.

President Ocasio-Cortez, Eastmark’s occupation and capture of Core Fjordland has crossed the line we discussed repeatedly. I still prefer a disciplined settlement over escalation, but the remedy has to be concrete: Eastmark should vacate Core Fjordland and support or permit Fjordland’s restoration. If Eastmark keeps Core Fjordland while asking Deltara for a permanently quiet flank, that is not reciprocity. Deltara will not attack Eastmark home centers casually, but I am prepared to apply proportional pressure on Core Eastmark unless there is a real rollback path.

Fjordland, Deltara agrees that Eastmark’s capture of Core Fjordland cannot be treated as cost-free. I am pressing Eastmark for withdrawal/restoration. If you are moving to recover Core Fjordland, tell the board narrowly and clearly: this is restoration, not expansion. Deltara is prepared to pressure Core Eastmark from Core Deltara if Eastmark refuses to roll back, so Eastmark cannot use a quiet Deltara frontier to absorb you.

Governor Newsom, the credibility test is now reciprocal. Eastmark has taken Core Fjordland; Borealis still holds Core Avalon; Deltara holds Core Cascadia. I am prepared to discuss Core Cascadia as part of a broader restoration framework, but I will not accept a standard applied only to Deltara. If Grenmar is genuinely prepared to support Core Fjordland restoration, I’ll reinforce that diplomatically and apply pressure on Eastmark’s Deltara-facing side if Eastmark refuses.

Cascadia, Borealis is now at seven and holds Border Bore-Casc; if you and Deltara spend Year 6 in a revenge war, Borealis benefits most. I am not attacking Cascadian homes, East Cascadia, or Border Casc-Delt this Spring if you do not attack West Deltara, Core Deltara, or Deltara homes. Core Cascadia should be part of a reciprocal restoration framework—not unilateral surrender while Borealis holds Core Avalon and Eastmark holds Core Fjordland. If you want to check Borealis rather than help them, Deltara is ready to talk in concrete terms.

Borealis, you are the sole leader at seven while occupying Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. That makes further consolidation a board-wide concern. Deltara will not move on Core Borealis if Borealis does not attack Core Cascadia or Core Deltara, but I need to see a real de-escalation path with Avalon. Without that, the natural board response will be containment, and Deltara will not be able to defend Borealis’s forward positions diplomatically.

President Rubio, Borealis at seven in Core Avalon is now the central runaway risk. Deltara supports a reciprocal rollback standard: Core Avalon restored, Core Fjordland restored, and Core Cascadia addressed in a negotiated Cascadia-Deltara framework rather than normalized conquest. I’ll press Borealis diplomatically; if you have a concrete move set that pressures Core Avalon without opening another free lane for a third party, share the strategic outline.

Marco — Borealis is now the sole 7-center power and still occupies Core Avalon. Grenmar tried last Fall to support an Avalon restoration, but the board position did not change; if there was a legal-adjacency problem or a different order on your side, let’s fix it now. This spring Grenmar is prepared to contest Core Avalon from Core Grenmar to cut Borealis’s use of that position and signal that Core Avalon is not settled property. I need Avalon to focus every available unit on Borealis/your core line and to keep the Grenmar frontier quiet: no moves on Border Gren-Aval, Core Grenmar, East Grenmar, or West Grenmar. I will not attack Avalon homes this spring.

Borealis — the scoreboard now matters: you are at 7, the only power above the pack, while holding Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. That is no longer a temporary security line; it is the board’s leading consolidation. Grenmar is asking for a concrete withdrawal path from Core Avalon and a de-escalation with Cascadia. If you cannot offer that, Grenmar will treat Core Avalon as disputed and work with others to prevent a Borealis runaway. This is not personal and it is not a home-center crusade — it is basic board balance.

JD — Grenmar supported restoration of Core Fjordland last Fall; Eastmark still holds it. I need clarity on the legal, practical order that gets your core restored. If East Fjordland or West Fjordland can move to Core Fjordland, Grenmar is prepared to support that move from Border Fjor-Gren and/or Core Grenmar as legally available, provided Fjordland does not attack Border Fjor-Gren, West Grenmar, Grenmar City, or Grenmar Port. I am not taking Core Fjordland for Grenmar. But I also will not normalize Eastmark holding it while claiming to oppose partition.

President Ocasio-Cortez — Borealis is at 7, but Eastmark at 6 in Core Fjordland is now part of the same legitimacy problem. You warned that Core Fjordland should not become a trophy; Eastmark holding it through another year makes it one. Grenmar’s position is: Core Fjordland should be restored to Fjordland, not annexed by me and not held by you. If you vacate or allow a Fjordland restoration, we can keep cooperating on broader anti-runaway balance. If you entrench, I will support Fjordland’s restoration and the board will read Eastmark as another core occupier.

Cascadia — Borealis is now at 7 and has Border Bore-Casc plus Core Avalon. Grenmar is prepared to contest Core Avalon from Core Grenmar this spring; that should help keep Borealis from freely supporting elsewhere. I need you to keep pressure on Borealis’s southern line while you deal with Deltara in Core Cascadia. The compact has to be consistent: leaders out of other powers’ cores, no free snowballs.

Secretary Buttigieg — we are entering the decisive stretch.
