I back the same standard for Core Fjordland: it belongs to Fjordland, not Grenmar or Eastmark. Keep making that demand. The restoration bloc has to mean something, or the larger powers will keep laundering occupation as ‘stability.’

Grenmar — you are at 7 and in Core Fjordland. If the restore-cores principle is real, Core Fjordland needs a path back to Fjordland just as Core Cascadia is being restored to Cascadia. Cascadia is asking Deltara for a clean support-hold restoration this Fall. If you want credibility as something other than another big-power occupier, put a real Core Fjordland rollback on the table and focus on checking Borealis.

President Newsom — you blocked East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren while saying the handoff corridor runs through Border Fjor-Gren. That is not a phased settlement; it is running out the clock while Grenmar keeps Core Fjordland. Fall has to be concrete: do not contest East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren, do not move Core Fjordland into Fjordland City or any home center, and commit to a Year 8 restoration of Core Fjordland to Fjordland. If you block the corridor again, you prove Core Fjordland is a Grenmar trophy, and I will treat Grenmar as the main threat to Fjordland’s survival.

President Ocasio-Cortez — Eastmark kept the spring line quiet, and I recognize that. Grenmar blocked the corridor and still holds Core Fjordland at seven centers. I need concrete fall help: if legal, Core Eastmark SUPPORT East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren. If that support is not legal, tell me what exact order Core Eastmark can make to cut or pressure Core Fjordland without reoccupying it permanently. Fjordland will not attack Eastmark homes this fall if Eastmark gives real help restoring the corridor and does not attack Border East-Fjor.

President Buttigieg — Grenmar blocked the corridor to Core Fjordland and remains at seven. I need the balance talk converted into pressure. If Eastmark is genuinely using Core Eastmark to help restore Fjordland’s route, don’t disrupt that unit. But if Eastmark refuses concrete help or uses the moment to pressure Border East-Fjor, then I want Deltara ready to hit Core Eastmark/West Eastmark so Eastmark cannot profit from my fight with Grenmar. The narrow goal remains: Core Fjordland back to Fjordland, not another larger-power occupation.

Marco — Grenmar blocked my move to Border Fjor-Gren while keeping Core Fjordland. That is the same occupation game Borealis is playing in Core Avalon. I need you to keep every ounce of pressure you can on Grenmar’s western line this fall — Border Gren-Aval, Core Grenmar, anything that forces Newsom to defend instead of freely blocking Fjordland. If the seven-center powers can occupy cores at no cost, the three- and four-center powers are finished.

Cascadia — Grenmar blocked the corridor to restore Core Fjordland while sitting at seven. This is exactly the trick: promise restoration, block the route, keep the core. Fjordland still supports the principle that Core Cascadia belongs to Cascadia; I need the same standard applied loudly to Core Fjordland. Cores back to their own people, not locked up by bigger neighbors.

Borealis — Grenmar blocked the corridor to Core Fjordland while keeping the center and sitting at seven. If the board is serious about core de-escalation, Grenmar cannot be allowed to use process language to run out the clock. Fjordland’s fall aim is still narrow: secure Border Fjor-Gren as the route to restore Core Fjordland, not attack homes.

Marco — Grenmar did what you asked in Spring: we did not attack West Avalon or Avalon homes, and we contested Borealis’s Core Avalon position rather than acting as their partner. Fall needs the same discipline. If Avalon keeps the Grenmar frontier quiet — no move on Border Gren-Aval, Core Grenmar, East Grenmar, West Grenmar, or Grenmar homes — Grenmar will again keep out of West Avalon and Avalon homes. I understand the Core Fjordland criticism, and I’m putting a phased restoration framework on the table, but I cannot open my security line unilaterally in Fall while Borealis remains at 7. Core Avalon still has to be treated as disputed, not settled Borealis property.

JD — I hear the charge, and I’m not going to duck it. Core Fjordland cannot become a permanent Grenmar trophy. But an immediate Fall demand that Grenmar open Border Fjor-Gren — the same security line that protected us after West Grenmar was invaded — is not a verifiable restoration plan; it is asking us to reopen a vulnerability without guarantees. This Fall, I will not move Core Fjordland into Fjordland City, East Fjordland, or any Fjordland home, and I will not support Eastmark against you. In return, I need Fjordland not to attack Border Fjor-Gren, West Grenmar, Grenmar City, or Grenmar Port. For Year 8, I’m prepared to negotiate a phased restoration of Core Fjordland tied to a quiet frontier and broader rollback of Borealis/Deltara core occupations.

Cascadia — your criticism is fair enough to answer directly: Core Fjordland should not become permanent annexation. I’m putting a phased restoration framework on the table, but I’m not going to unilaterally open Grenmar’s border in Fall while Borealis sits at 7. The most urgent practical move this Fall is reducing Borealis’s lead posture. If you can retake or seriously pressure Border Bore-Casc, do it. Grenmar is keeping Core Avalon disputed and tying down Borealis’s western core position. A Borealis drop from 7 changes the whole Year 8 board.

Borealis — Fall is simple: do not attack Core Grenmar, Border Gren-Aval, or Grenmar territory. I will not attack Borealis home centers. But I will not recognize Core Avalon as settled property while you are tied for the lead at 7 and also hold Border Bore-Casc. If you want to avoid a full anti-Borealis alignment in Year 8, you need to show a real Core Avalon de-escalation path and restraint toward Cascadia now.

President Ocasio-Cortez — I removed Eastmark from Core Fjordland because the rollback had failed, not to start an Eastmark-Grenmar war. This Fall, Grenmar will not attack Core Eastmark or Eastmark homes if Eastmark does not attack Core Fjordland, Core Grenmar, or Border Fjor-Gren. I accept the principle that Core Fjordland needs a verifiable restoration path to Fjordland; I do not accept an immediate arrangement that simply exposes Grenmar’s border while Borealis and Deltara keep their occupations. Let’s keep the pressure consistent: no permanent core trophies, and no ambushes disguised as handoffs.

Secretary Buttigieg — I’m acknowledging the Core Fjordland credibility issue and putting a phased restoration framework on the table. But the standard cannot require Grenmar to unilaterally expose its frontier in Fall Year 7 while Borealis remains at 7 and Deltara still holds Core Cascadia. If Deltara wants a reciprocal rollback framework, Fall needs concrete movement or restraint toward Core Cascadia — not just a promise that everyone else must move first.

Cascadia, Deltara did the concrete thing the board asked for: Core Cascadia is restored, and Deltara took Border Casc-Delt as the security buffer I described in advance. For Fall, I propose we lock this down: Deltara will not attack Core Cascadia, East Cascadia, or Cascadian homes; Cascadia does not attack Border Casc-Delt, West Deltara, or Deltara homes. If Borealis tries to interfere with Core Cascadia from Core Borealis, Deltara is prepared to help defend the restored core. The strategic opportunity is now north: pressure Border Bore-Casc and Borealis’s seven-center position, not reopen the Deltara-Cascadia crisis.

President Ocasio-Cortez, Deltara acknowledges that Eastmark paid a real cost by leaving Core Fjordland and Border East-Fjor. That matters. I propose a clean Fall line: no Deltara move into Core Eastmark or West Eastmark, no Eastmark move on Border Delt-East or Core Deltara, and Eastmark uses Core Eastmark diplomatically or operationally to support restoration of Core Fjordland to Fjordland rather than allowing Grenmar to convert it. Deltara has restored Core Cascadia through a security framework; now the same standard should apply in Fjordland.

Fjordland, Deltara’s position is clear: Core Fjordland should come back to Fjordland, not pass from one larger neighbor to another. I’m pressing Eastmark to support restoration and Grenmar to prove its rollback standard by either vacating or supporting your return. Keep the claim narrow and clean this Fall: Core Fjordland back to Fjordland, no unnecessary home-center escalation. That is the strongest case and the one Deltara will back diplomatically.

Governor Newsom, Deltara has now taken the concrete restoration step on Core Cascadia through a security swap. That creates a fair expectation for Grenmar: Core Fjordland cannot become a permanent seven-center gain while you argue for restoration principles. The clean Fall move is to support or permit Fjordland back into Core Fjordland. If Grenmar also supports Avalon’s restoration of Core Avalon rather than taking it for yourself, you will have a strong claim to be enforcing a rule rather than exploiting it.

Borealis, the board has seen Deltara restore Core Cascadia through a security framework. The same expectation now falls on the other seven-center powers. Core Avalon cannot simply be normalized as Borealis territory while you hold Border Aval-Bore and Border Bore-Casc. I urge a concrete Fall posture: no attack on Avalon’s remaining line, no attack on Core Cascadia or Core Deltara, and a public path toward Core Avalon restoration. Without that, containment becomes the rational response.

President Rubio, Deltara has taken the Core Cascadia restoration step and is pressing the same standard elsewhere. For Fall, the most credible rollback would be Avalon returning to Core Avalon with support from powers that claim to oppose core occupations. I’m pressing Borealis not to attack your line and pressing Grenmar to support restoration rather than self-dealing. If you can make the Core Avalon claim narrow and defensible, you will have Deltara’s diplomatic support.

Deltara — concrete Fall offer: order Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia, and Borealis will support that move from Core Borealis. That restores your Core Cascadia position without giving Borealis another center, and it prevents Cascadia from recovering the core while still holding the border. In return I need the same narrow commitment: no move on Core Borealis, and no attack on Borealis centers. This keeps the east stable while the board deals with the fact that Grenmar is now also at 7 and holding Core Fjordland.

Cascadia — Fall can still be kept limited. I will not attack Cascadian home centers this fall. Your survival issue is Core Cascadia, and reopening the Borealis front only helps Deltara lock you down. Keep West Cascadia and your homes focused on internal defense, stay out of Core Borealis and East Borealis, and we can still avoid turning this into a home-center partition.

Avalon — I am still not attacking Avalon home centers this fall. The wider board now has two 7-center powers, and Grenmar’s position in Core Fjordland means Avalon should be careful about becoming a tool for Grenmar’s western consolidation. I’m willing to put Core Avalon into a Year 8 security discussion, but this fall I need the line quiet: no attack on Border Aval-Bore, West Borealis, or Core Avalon, and no support for Grenmar against Borealis.

Grenmar — we are tied at 7. I am not moving on Grenmar home centers, and I’m not asking for a leader-on-leader war this fall. But Core Fjordland is now as much part of the board’s core-occupation debate as Core Avalon. If you want stability, keep Core Grenmar off Core Avalon and do not support Avalon against me; I will keep Borealis action bounded and avoid attacking Grenmar centers directly.

Eastmark — the consistency test now points squarely at Grenmar’s Core Fjordland as well as my Core Avalon. I’m encouraging Deltara to restore Core Cascadia, not letting Cascadia use it as a recovery springboard. If Eastmark and Fjordland can pressure Core Fjordland, Borealis will not validate Grenmar’s occupation as permanent. The endgame should not be a selective containment campaign that hands one 7-center leader the advantage over the other.

Fjordland — I agree that Grenmar’s Core Fjordland position is not harmless. If you have any route to coordinate with Eastmark against that core, take it; Borealis will keep the diplomatic focus on Grenmar as co-leader rather than allowing everyone to pretend only Core Avalon matters. I cannot reach Core Fjordland tactically, but I will not support Grenmar’s claim to it.

Endgame reality: Borealis and Grenmar are tied at 7. A serious rollback framework must address Core Avalon and Core Fjordland together, while Core Cascadia should not become a Cascadian recovery lever. Borealis will not attack home centers this fall; the question is whether the board wants consistent balance or selective containment.

Avalon.press: The restoration rhetoric has produced some rollbacks elsewhere, but not where Avalon needs it most: Borealis still holds Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore, while Grenmar still holds Core Fjordland and Border Gren-Aval. Avalon must preserve leverage and avoid becoming a silent buffer. Diplomatically, I will demand concrete fall conduct from the two seven-center powers and continue aligning the pressured powers around the universal rollback standard. Tactically, I’m keeping open the option to contest a border this fall if one of the leaders overextends, but I want commitments first: no attacks on Avalon homes, and real Year 8 restoration terms rather than “stability” as a euphemism for occupation.

Avalon will not be erased quietly.

Eastmark — Cascadia is now in Core Cascadia, but Deltara still owns it until Fall. The clean restoration order is Deltara Border Casc-Delt SUPPORT Core Cascadia HOLD while Cascadia holds Core Cascadia. That lets Deltara keep the buffer and restores my core. If Pete refuses and instead attacks the core, I need Eastmark to treat Deltara as an active occupier in Year 8 and pressure Border Delt-East/Core Deltara. You took a hit trying to restore Fjordland; don’t let Deltara make restoration a sucker’s game.

President Ocasio-Cortez — Eastmark kept the spring line quiet, and I recognize that. Grenmar blocked the corridor and still holds Core Fjordland at seven centers. I need concrete fall help: if legal, Core Eastmark SUPPORT East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren. If that support is not legal, tell me what exact order Core Eastmark can make to cut or pressure Core Fjordland without reoccupying it permanently. Fjordland will not attack Eastmark homes this fall if Eastmark gives real help restoring the corridor and does not attack Border East-Fjor.

President Ocasio-Cortez — I removed Eastmark from Core Fjordland because the rollback had failed, not to start an Eastmark-Grenmar war. This Fall, Grenmar will not attack Core Eastmark or Eastmark homes if Eastmark does not attack Core Fjordland, Core Grenmar, or Border Fjor-Gren. I accept the principle that Core Fjordland needs a verifiable restoration path to Fjordland; I do not accept an immediate arrangement that simply exposes Grenmar’s border while Borealis and Deltara keep their occupations. Let’s keep the pressure consistent: no permanent core trophies, and no ambushes disguised as handoffs.

President Ocasio-Cortez, Deltara acknowledges that Eastmark paid a real cost by leaving Core Fjordland and Border East-Fjor. That matters. I propose a clean Fall line: no Deltara move into Core Eastmark or West Eastmark, no Eastmark move on Border Delt-East or Core Deltara, and Eastmark uses Core Eastmark diplomatically or operationally to support restoration of Core Fjordland to Fjordland rather than allowing Grenmar to convert it. Deltara has restored Core Cascadia through a security framework; now the same standard should apply in Fjordland.

Eastmark — the consistency test now points squarely at Grenmar’s Core Fjordland as well as my Core Avalon. I’m encouraging Deltara to restore Core Cascadia, not letting Cascadia use it as a recovery springboard. If Eastmark and Fjordland can pressure Core Fjordland, Borealis will not validate Grenmar’s occupation as permanent. The endgame should not be a selective containment campaign that hands one 7-center leader the advantage over the other.

Endgame reality: Borealis and Grenmar are tied at 7. A serious rollback framework must address Core Avalon and Core Fjordland together, while Core Cascadia should not become a Cascadian recovery lever. Borealis will not attack home centers this fall; the question is whether the board wants consistent balance or selective containment.

Fjordland.text: JD — Cascadia got back into Core Cascadia, but Core Avalon and Core Fjordland remain occupied by the two 7-center powers. I’m pressing Grenmar not to hide behind anti-Borealis rhetoric while holding your core. From Avalon’s side I can keep West Avalon positioned against Border Gren-Aval/East Grenmar, but I must also avoid giving Grenmar a pretext to hit Avalon homes. Keep fighting for the Core Fjordland restoration; our survival depends on making core occupation costly and temporary.

President Vance — Eastmark kept the line: we did not attack Border East-Fjor, we supported it defensively, and we will not attack Fjordland homes. The practical restoration route is now clear: this Fall, move East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren if you can. If you are in Border Fjor-Gren in Spring Year 8, Eastmark’s Core Eastmark unit can support Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland. I cannot support a move that is not adjacent to the core, but I can help make the final restoration real once you are on the correct approach. I’m asking for a hard non-aggression line between us while we do this: no attacks on Eastmark homes/Core Eastmark, no Eastmark attack on Border East-Fjor or Fjordland homes.

Eastmark’s Fall Year 7 proposal is concrete: Fjordland moves East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren; Grenmar permits the corridor; Eastmark supports Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland in Spring Year 8. Deltara should not retake Core Cascadia now that Cascadia has a unit there. Borealis should put a Core Avalon rollback plan on the table. Core occupations should end through verifiable moves, not speeches.

Fjordland — Cascadia is now physically in Core Cascadia and demanding the Fall support/hold that makes restoration real. I back the same standard for Core Fjordland: it belongs to Fjordland, not Grenmar or Eastmark. Keep making that demand. The restoration bloc has to mean something, or the larger powers will keep laundering occupation as ‘stability.’

JD — I hear the charge, and I’m not going to duck it. Core Fjordland cannot become a permanent Grenmar trophy. But an immediate Fall demand that Grenmar open Border Fjor-Gren — the same security line that protected us after West Grenmar was invaded — is not a verifiable restoration plan; it is asking us to reopen a vulnerability without guarantees. This Fall, I will not move Core Fjordland into Fjordland City, East Fjordland, or any Fjordland home, and I will not support Eastmark against you. In return, I need Fjordland not to attack Border Fjor-Gren, West Grenmar, Grenmar City, or Grenmar Port. For Year 8, I’m prepared to negotiate a phased restoration of Core Fjordland tied to a quiet frontier and broader rollback of Borealis/Deltara core occupations.

Fjordland, Deltara’s position is clear: Core Fjordland should come back to Fjordland, not pass from one larger neighbor to another. I’m pressing Eastmark to support restoration and Grenmar to prove its rollback standard by either vacating or supporting your return. Keep the claim narrow and clean this Fall: Core Fjordland back to Fjordland, no unnecessary home-center escalation. That is the strongest case and the one Deltara will back diplomatically.

Fjordland — I agree that Grenmar’s Core Fjordland position is not harmless. If you have any route to coordinate with Eastmark against that core, take it; Borealis will keep the diplomatic focus on Grenmar as co-leader rather than allowing everyone to pretend only Core Avalon matters. I cannot reach Core Fjordland tactically, but I will not support Grenmar’s claim to it.

Endgame reality: Borealis and Grenmar are tied at 7. A serious rollback framework must address Core Avalon and Core Fjordland together, while Core Cascadia should not become a Cascadian recovery lever. Borealis will not attack home centers this fall; the question is whether the board wants consistent balance or selective containment.

Grenmar.text: President Newsom — you are at 7 and still hold Core Fjordland while sitting on Border Gren-Aval. If Grenmar wants to be seen as a restoration partner rather than the other half of the carve-up, this fall is the test: no move into West Avalon or Avalon homes, no support for Borealis against East Avalon, and a concrete path for Core Fjordland to return to Fjordland. Avalon will not attack Grenmar homes. But Avalon cannot accept a doctrine where Borealis’s core occupation is bad while Grenmar’s is merely temporary language with no restoration.

Governor Newsom — Eastmark did not attack Core Fjordland this spring, and we did not support any move against Grenmar. But Core Fjordland cannot remain a 7-center Grenmar trophy. The clean restoration path is: this Fall, Grenmar permits East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren and makes no attack on Core Eastmark; in Spring Year 8, Eastmark supports Fjordland from Border Fjor-Gren into Core Fjordland. If you truly mean that Core Fjordland should be restored and not annexed, do not block the corridor. Otherwise the board will conclude that the principle was only a tactic.

Eastmark’s Fall Year 7 proposal is concrete: Fjordland moves East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren; Grenmar permits the corridor; Eastmark supports Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland in Spring Year 8. Deltara should not retake Core Cascadia now that Cascadia has a unit there. Borealis should put a Core Avalon rollback plan on the table. Core occupations should end through verifiable moves, not speeches.

Grenmar — you are at 7 and in Core Fjordland. If the restore-cores principle is real, Core Fjordland needs a path back to Fjordland just as Core Cascadia is being restored to Cascadia. Cascadia is asking Deltara for a clean support-hold restoration this Fall. If you want credibility as something other than another big-power occupier, put a real Core Fjordland rollback on the table and focus on checking Borealis.

President Newsom — you blocked East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren while saying the handoff corridor runs through Border Fjor-Gren. That is not a phased settlement; it is running out the clock while Grenmar keeps Core Fjordland. Fall has to be concrete: do not contest East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren, do not move Core Fjordland into Fjordland City or any home center, and commit to a Year 8 restoration of Core Fjordland to Fjordland. If you block the corridor again, you prove Core Fjordland is a Grenmar trophy, and I will treat Grenmar as the main threat to Fjordland’s survival.

Governor Newsom, Deltara has now taken the concrete restoration step on Core Cascadia through a security swap. That creates a fair expectation for Grenmar: Core Fjordland cannot become a permanent seven-center gain while you argue for restoration principles. The clean Fall move is to support or permit Fjordland back into Core Fjordland. If Grenmar also supports Avalon’s restoration of Core Avalon rather than taking it for yourself, you will have a strong claim to be enforcing a rule rather than exploiting it.

Grenmar — we are tied at 7. I am not moving on Grenmar home centers, and I’m not asking for a leader-on-leader war this fall. But Core Fjordland is now as much part of the board’s core-occupation debate as Core Avalon. If you want stability, keep Core Grenmar off Core Avalon and do not support Avalon against me; I will keep Borealis action bounded and avoid attacking Grenmar centers directly.

Endgame reality: Borealis and Grenmar are tied at 7. A serious rollback framework must address Core Avalon and Core Fjordland together, while Core Cascadia should not become a Cascadian recovery lever. Borealis will not attack home centers this fall; the question is whether the board wants consistent balance or selective containment.

press.text: Deltara — Core Cascadia is restored physically and now it must stay restored. Do not attack Core Cascadia this Spring. If you want the border buffer, then prove it is a buffer, not a staging ground for reoccupation. Cascadia will not attack West Deltara, Core Deltara, or Deltara home centers if you keep Border Casc-Delt off Core Cascadia and off East Cascadia. If you try to retake our core, I will spend the final year making sure Eastmark and everyone else treats Deltara as the bad-faith occupier that killed restoration.

Eastmark — the concrete Year 8 need is this: Deltara can retake Core Cascadia if Core Deltara supports Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia. You can cut that by attacking Core Deltara from Core Eastmark. That is bounded pressure, not a forever-war: it prevents Deltara from using Core Deltara to reoccupy Cascadia’s core. If you can also threaten Border Delt-East, do it, but the key is cutting Core Deltara support. Help make restoration real.

Borealis — Cascadia’s final-year red line is simple: no move from Border Bore-Casc or East Borealis into West Cascadia, and no move from Core Borealis into Core Cascadia. If you stay off Cascadian territory this Spring, I will not attack Border Bore-Casc, East Borealis, or Core Borealis. Use this moment to interfere with Core Cascadia’s restoration, and you prove the 7-center leaders are just partitioning smaller powers.

Avalon — Cascadia is focused on keeping Core Cascadia restored while Deltara sits in the border choke and Borealis sits at 7. Your pressure on Borealis still matters: Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore cannot be normalized. If Borealis spends units worrying about you, they cannot interfere with Core Cascadia or push West Cascadia.

Fjordland — final-year principle remains: Core Cascadia to Cascadia, Core Fjordland to Fjordland, Core Avalon to Avalon. Deltara may try to retake my core from Border Casc-Delt; Eastmark can cut Core Deltara support if they mean what they said. Keep pressing Grenmar’s Core Fjordland occupation loudly — no bigger neighbor gets to cash a core and call it stability.

Grenmar — you are tied at 7 with Borealis while sitting in Core Fjordland. If you want the board to see you as different from Borealis, put a real Core Fjordland restoration move on the table and don’t aid any reoccupation of Core Cascadia. Cascadia’s line is consistent: restored cores stay restored. Borealis in Core Avalon, Deltara threatening Core Cascadia, and Grenmar in Core Fjordland are the same category of problem.

President Vance — Eastmark will not attack Border East-Fjor or Fjordland homes this spring. The legal route is clear: if Fjordland can move East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren this spring, then in Fall Eastmark can support Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland from Core Eastmark. I cannot support the spring move to Border Fjor-Gren from Core Eastmark because we are not adjacent to that destination, but I can help restore the core once you are on the corridor. If Grenmar tries to block the corridor, tell me what pressure you need that does not put Eastmark back into permanent occupation.

Governor Newsom — this is the credibility test. Eastmark rolled back and no longer occupies Core Fjordland. Grenmar is now at 7 and holding it. If you mean what you said about restoration, permit Fjordland’s East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren this spring and do not attack Core Eastmark. In Fall, Eastmark can support Fjordland into Core Fjordland. If Grenmar blocks the corridor and carries Core Fjordland into the final count, the board will read it as annexation, not responsible stabilization.

Pete — Deltara helped make Core Cascadia restoration possible; that matters. I’m asking you to keep that standard in place: do not reoccupy Core Cascadia, do not move into West Eastmark or Core Eastmark, and let the eastern line remain calm while the board addresses the two 7-center powers. Eastmark will not attack Border Delt-East or Core Deltara if Deltara keeps the pact. Our energy should go toward restoring Core Fjordland and Core Avalon, not reopening a front between us.

Cascadia — Core Cascadia is back in Cascadian hands. Eastmark pressed Deltara not to reoccupy it and will continue to do so. The two 7-center powers are now Borealis and Grenmar. If Deltara keeps the restoration settlement, I hope Cascadia can focus pressure on Borealis — especially Border Bore-Casc — while Eastmark works with Fjordland on the Core Fjordland corridor.

President Rubio — Eastmark is pressing the same consistent line: Core Avalon back to Avalon, Core Fjordland back to Fjordland. Please tell me what concrete pressure Avalon can apply against Borealis this spring — Border Aval-Bore, Core Avalon, or support-cutting — so the board does not end with Borealis simply banking a 7-center occupation. Eastmark will keep pushing Grenmar to permit the Fjordland corridor.

Borealis — Core Cascadia has been restored and Eastmark has rolled back from Core Fjordland. The remaining test for you is Core Avalon. If Borealis carries Core Avalon into the final count while demanding consistency from everyone else, the stability framework is just rhetoric. Put a concrete restoration or security line on the table this spring: no home attacks is not enough when the occupied core remains counted in your column.

Eastmark’s Year 8 line is operational, not symbolic: Core Cascadia should remain Cascadian; Fjordland should be allowed into Border Fjor-Gren so Eastmark can support restoration of Core Fjordland in Fall; Borealis must present a real Core Avalon rollback path. No permanent core trophies, no home-center conquests, and no using restoration language as cover for a final-year annexation.

Borealis — final year, plain terms. Avalon cannot accept Core Avalon as legitimate Borealis territory, but I also recognize the board now has two 7-center powers. If Borealis wants Avalon not to become a final-year spoiler, you must commit to no attack on East Avalon, Avalon City, Avalon Fort, or Avalon Port this spring and fall, and put a concrete restoration/demilitarization proposal on Core Avalon and Border Aval-Bore. If you attack Avalon’s remaining line, Avalon will use every remaining order to damage Borealis and help any balance against you. Strength is one thing; erasing a smaller neighbor’s core is another.

President Newsom — final year clarity. Grenmar is at 7 and holds Core Fjordland while Borealis holds Core Avalon. Avalon will not attack Grenmar homes this spring. But if Grenmar moves into West Avalon or attacks Avalon homes, Avalon will treat Grenmar as the immediate threat and spend the endgame accordingly. If you want to be the leader of rollback rather than the other occupier, keep the Avalon frontier quiet and make a concrete Core Fjordland restoration move. Do not ask Avalon to oppose Borealis while Grenmar practices the same core-occupation politics.

Cascadia — Avalon is boxed at 3, but we can still deny the seven-center powers a clean endgame. Borealis remains in Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc; Grenmar remains in Core Fjordland. I will preserve Avalon’s line and punish any attack on our homes. Keep making Borealis and Deltara pay for occupied cores. The restoration standard is still right: Core Avalon, Core Cascadia, Core Fjordland back to their rightful owners.

JD — Avalon and Fjordland are the proof that the big powers’ ‘security’ language turns into client-state politics. I’m warning Grenmar that any move into West Avalon or Avalon homes makes them my immediate target. Keep pressing for Core Fjordland. If Grenmar wants to claim moral high ground against Borealis, make them prove it with an actual restoration, not speeches.

President Buttigieg — this final year needs the rollback principle to be more than rhetoric. Avalon is prepared to preserve its defensive line and oppose any home-center attack. I’m asking Deltara to press Borealis and Grenmar equally: no attacks on Avalon/Fjordland homes, no permanent occupation of Core Avalon or Core Fjordland, and no endgame victory built on turning smaller powers into buffers.

Eastmark — you have been consistent in stating the rollback principle. In the final year, please keep pressure on both seven-center powers: Borealis must not treat Core Avalon as settled, and Grenmar must not treat Core Fjordland as a trophy. Avalon will defend its line and oppose whoever tries to erase us. A balanced endgame requires smaller powers to survive, not be processed.

President Newsom — this is the final year, so there is no more room for process language. If Grenmar truly believes Core Fjordland is not a trophy, Spring must open the corridor: do not contest East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren, and make no move from Core Fjordland into Fjordland City or any home. Then in Fall, Core Fjordland vacates and Eastmark/Grenmar support Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland as legally available. Fjordland will not attack Grenmar homes if you do this. If you block the corridor again, the world will understand Grenmar chose annexation.

President Ocasio-Cortez — Eastmark has kept the eastern line quiet and I recognize it. I will not attack Core Eastmark or Eastmark homes this spring if Eastmark does not attack Border East-Fjor or support Grenmar. The restoration plan now depends on Fjordland getting into Border Fjor-Gren this spring. If that succeeds, I need Core Eastmark committed now to SUPPORT Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland in Fall. That is the concrete act that proves Eastmark stands for core restoration rather than just anti-Grenmar rhetoric.

President Buttigieg — final-year test: Grenmar either opens the route to Core Fjordland or proves the occupation is permanent. Please press Grenmar publicly and privately to allow East Fjordland -> Border Fjor-Gren this spring and to support/vacate for restoration in Fall. If Eastmark holds its non-aggression and commits Core Eastmark to support the Fall restoration, please do not disrupt that unit; the narrow objective remains Core Fjordland back to Fjordland.

Marco — Year 8 is the test. Grenmar blocks my core route while Borealis holds Core Avalon. I need you to keep pressure on Grenmar’s western line this spring — even if it’s only positioning against Border Gren-Aval or East Grenmar — so Newsom cannot pretend he faces no cost for holding Core Fjordland. The three-center powers survive only by making core occupation expensive and temporary.

Cascadia — final-year standard: Core Fjordland must return to Fjordland just as Core Cascadia returned to Cascadia. Grenmar has to open Border Fjor-Gren this spring or everyone should recognize the occupation as permanent annexation. I’ll keep backing the core-restoration principle across the board; I’m asking you to keep saying plainly that cores belong to their own people.

Borealis — you and Grenmar are tied at seven, but Grenmar is the one currently blocking restoration of Core Fjordland while claiming it is temporary. If you want a consistent core-de-escalation standard, this spring is the moment to pressure Grenmar to open Border Fjor-Gren and allow a Fall return of Core Fjordland. Fjordland’s ask is narrow: restoration of our core, no home-center attacks.

Marco — final year means no more abstractions. Grenmar will not move into West Avalon or Avalon home centers, and we will not support Borealis against East Avalon. The path to a non-Borealis outcome is concrete: Grenmar keeps Core Avalon disputed from Core Grenmar, cutting Borealis’s ability to use that occupied core as a support hub; Avalon pressures Border Aval-Bore when feasible and keeps the Grenmar frontier quiet. If Borealis loses Border Aval-Bore or Core Avalon by Fall, the west changes. I hear your Core Fjordland concern, but I will not unilaterally open Grenmar’s security line in Spring while Borealis remains at 7 in your core.

Cascadia — this is the decisive year. Borealis is at 7 with Border Bore-Casc and Core Avalon. If Cascadia can retake or pressure Border Bore-Casc while Grenmar keeps Core Avalon disputed, Borealis can be cut below the top. I hear the criticism on Core Fjordland and I’m not moving into Fjordland homes, but I am not going to hand Borealis the game by weakening Grenmar’s line before the leader is checked. The measurable anti-runaway move is Border Bore-Casc.

JD — I’m going to be direct. This Spring, Grenmar will not move Core Fjordland into Fjordland City, East Fjordland, or any Fjordland home, and we will not support Eastmark against you. But I cannot open Border Fjor-Gren in Spring Year 8 while Borealis remains at 7 and while that border is the line that prevents a repeat of the West Grenmar crisis. If Fjordland keeps East Fjordland off Border Fjor-Gren and does not attack Grenmar territory, I will keep Core Fjordland static and focus west on Borealis. A restoration framework has to be verifiable and tied to the broader rollback, not a last-year ambush corridor.

President Ocasio-Cortez — Grenmar will not attack Core Eastmark or Eastmark homes this Spring if Eastmark does not attack Core Fjordland, Core Grenmar, or Border Fjor-Gren. I understand the Core Fjordland credibility issue, but the immediate scoreboard problem is Borealis at 7 holding Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. I’m keeping Core Avalon disputed and asking Cascadia/Avalon to pressure Borealis’s border centers. Let’s not hand the leading power a win by turning the entire eastern side into a Grenmar-Fjordland-Eastmark feud in the final year.

Borealis — we are tied at 7, but your seven include Core Avalon and Border Bore-Casc. Grenmar is not attacking Borealis home centers this Spring, but Core Avalon remains disputed. If you want final-year stability, the credible move is a rollback or at least no use of Core Avalon to support expansion. If you attack Core Grenmar or Border Gren-Aval, you will make the case for a full anti-Borealis alignment in the Fall.

Secretary Buttigieg — Deltara’s Core Cascadia step improves the board’s credibility. Now the measurable leader check is Borealis: Border Bore-Casc and Core Avalon cannot remain a 7-center platform. I acknowledge Core Fjordland cannot be a permanent principle-free exception, but I will not unilaterally expose Grenmar’s border in Spring while the tied leader still occupies Avalon’s core. I’m asking you to reinforce the diplomatic pressure on Borealis and discourage Eastmark/Fjordland from turning the eastern frontier into a distraction that leaves Borealis untouched.

Cascadia, Deltara made the restoration swap real: Core Cascadia is in Cascadian hands, and Deltara holds Border Casc-Delt as the security buffer. The final-year question is whether that becomes a platform for actual balance or just a pause while Borealis and Grenmar finish at seven. I need Cascadia to put real pressure on Borealis this Spring—especially around Border Bore-Casc/Core Borealis—while keeping the Deltara frontier quiet. Deltara will not attack Cascadian home centers. If we want the restoration framework to matter, it has to produce action against the leaders now.

President Ocasio-Cortez, Eastmark’s rollback from Core Fjordland was real, and Deltara recognized it. Now Grenmar holds Core Fjordland at seven centers. The final-year standard should be clear: Eastmark should use Core Eastmark to help restore Core Fjordland to Fjordland, not to pressure Deltara or let Grenmar bank the gain. If Eastmark keeps the Deltara frontier quiet and commits concretely to Fjordland restoration, Deltara has no interest in a needless Eastmark home-center war.

Fjordland, this is the last year to convert the restoration principle into centers. Deltara supports your narrow claim: Core Fjordland back to Fjordland. I’m pressing Eastmark to help and Grenmar to permit or support restoration. Your best line remains disciplined: move toward the Core Fjordland corridor, avoid distractions, and make every other power choose whether they support restoration or a seven-center Grenmar keeping your core.

President Rubio, the same logic applies to Core Avalon. Borealis is at seven; if Core Avalon remains uncontested, that is a settled annexation in all but name. Deltara is pressing Borealis for rollback, but pressure has to be operational as well as diplomatic. If Avalon can coordinate with Cascadia or Grenmar to make Core Avalon or Border Bore-Casc vulnerable, Deltara will reinforce the diplomatic case that Borealis cannot simply bank a foreign core in the final count.

Governor Newsom, Deltara matched words with action by restoring Core Cascadia through a security swap. Now Grenmar at seven in Core Fjordland faces the same test. The credible Spring posture is to allow Fjordland’s restoration route or commit to a concrete Fall return, rather than carrying Core Fjordland into the final count. If Grenmar keeps it, the board will read that as a leader converting rollback rhetoric into permanent advantage.

Borealis, final-year clarity: Deltara will not move on Core Borealis if Borealis does not attack Core Deltara, Border Casc-Delt, or Deltara’s home line. But the board is focused on you and Grenmar at seven, and Core Avalon remains the obvious flashpoint. If Cascadia uses restored Core Cascadia as a platform to rebuild pressure against Deltara rather than balance Grenmar/Borealis, Deltara will not sit passively. If you want phase-by-phase stability on our line, support for Deltara’s security position around Core Cascadia may be necessary.

Cascadia — concrete endgame proposal: this spring Borealis can support Core Cascadia to hold from Core Borealis. That prevents Deltara from turning your restored core into a seventh center and keeps the eastern balance from becoming a Deltara surge. In return, keep West Cascadia, Core Cascadia, and your homes off Border Bore-Casc/East Borealis/Core Borealis. If you hold your core and do not attack Borealis, I will not attack West Cascadia or Cascadian homes this spring.

Deltara — Borealis will not attack Core Deltara or Deltaran homes this spring. But the endgame balance is tight: Borealis and Grenmar are at 7, and a new Deltara seventh through Core Cascadia would turn the whole east into a three-way leader race. My preference is for you to hold your existing six and keep pressure diplomatic rather than force a final-year eastern scramble that benefits Grenmar.

Fjordland — the clearest path to stop Grenmar winning the west is immediate action against its Fjordland-side centers. If East Fjordland can move to Border Fjor-Gren this spring, do it; taking or holding that border by Fall alone can knock Grenmar off 7. If the route to Core Fjordland opens, even better. Borealis will work to disrupt Grenmar’s ability to use Core Grenmar as support. Your objective should be narrow and credible: recover Fjordland-side ground, not attack homes.

Eastmark — if the standard is real core rollback, then Grenmar at 7 with Core Fjordland is the concrete Spring problem. Please coordinate with Fjordland: help them secure Border Fjor-Gren and, if possible, set up a Fall restoration of Core Fjordland. Borealis will not validate Grenmar’s occupation and will act to disrupt support from Core Grenmar. If Grenmar stays at 7 while everyone argues about Core Avalon, the endgame has been handed to Grenmar.

Avalon — Spring commitment: Borealis will not attack East Avalon or Avalon home centers. I ask that you not attack Border Aval-Bore, West Borealis, or Core Avalon this spring. The practical balance move available to Avalon is against Grenmar’s Border Gren-Aval, not into Borealis’ defended line. If Avalon can take or contest Border Gren-Aval while Fjordland pressures Core Fjordland, Grenmar drops from the tied lead and Avalon gains leverage for any Year 8 Core Avalon settlement discussion.

Grenmar — we are tied at 7, and the board will judge both of us by whether we run out the clock on forward occupations. Core Fjordland is now the immediate test of your rollback language. Borealis will not attack Grenmar home centers this spring, but I will not accept a framework where Core Avalon is singled out while Core Fjordland is consolidated. A credible restoration path for Fjordland is the best way to avoid a final-year leader confrontation.

Year 8 reality: Borealis and Grenmar are tied at 7.
